This is an issue of accessibility depending on your environment. I work for $15 an hour, as a freelancer doing subcontracting work in Korea, so I mostly see the worst of the worst. In that context, AI code quality feels like a huge improvement.

Because in closed source codebases, there's plenty of low quality code.

In contrast, open source projects tend to curate only the best code, driven by visibility and reputation. I think that difference is significant.

You might not agree with me. And that's fine. We all have our own value systems. I don't agree with you, and you probably don't agree with me. That's a natural consequence of us being different people.

But here's what I think: I respect you, but our views can differ. I think your point is valid in certain contexts, but I stand by mine.


Can you give an example of a pattern that was considered common practice in a book 10 to 15 years ago that would be considered low-quality code today?

My experience is pretty much the reverse: that we seem to just go round and round relearning the lessons that had already been learned in the past.


And the 'monad' that functional programmers always talk about—same story. In C#, they encourage monadic composition by chaining errors. But about 15 years ago, that wasn't the case.

Back then, if there was no value → null. Now, even the absence of a value is modeled with Option, Maybe, or nullable types. Failures are handled not with throw/try-catch but with Result, Either, or Try.

Overall, we've shifted toward a style where we preserve the computation context and then compose the next computation. Instead of manually branching every time, now we use map, bind, or LINQ-style operations that define the composition rules.

Things that used to be used only by a small group of people eventually become embedded into the language itself.

For example, callbacks have evolved into Task, Promise, and async/await.

So honestly, I don't think quality has declined at all. I think there's just more context to keep track of now. I've seen around 40 different company codebases. I have no idea about US code, but I've seen code from Korean and Chinese large corporations, and the difference between past and present code is quite significant.


Right, there were examples like Singleton and baseController. We moved from ambient/global dependency access to explicit constructor injection and Composition Root, didn't we?

Application entry points use Composition Root now, but old general programming books didn't. Errors were handled differently too. In the past, you'd throw new Exception() and wrap it in try/catch at a higher level, but these days we use Result<T, E> type modeling. Of course, C# still uses try/catch, but the guidance in .NET has long been to return predictable failures as type contracts.

Old .NET documentation used to encourage global access to common features and dependencies. Now it's shifted toward composition at the entry point.

Node.js used to use nested error-first callbacks as a standard pattern, but that's no longer the case, right? It moved to promise/async-await, and these days, as you know, type-based modeling is trending.

C# books also used to return null if something was missing, but now we use nullable reference types to express nullability more explicitly.

Even inheritance—these days it's often advised to avoid inheritance, but it used to be very common.

Just off the top of my head, I can think of quite a few examples. Record keywords and immutability features started appearing about 10 years ago, and Java has started adopting them too.

These are all outdated patterns now, with clearly defined use cases. More precisely, the contexts in which they should be used have become much more granular.

I could probably give about 30 more examples of this.


I feel like the industry has learned a lot of good lessons from functional programming, and that has been reflected by functional features being baked into almost every popular imperative language.


I think this is a complex issue.

If there were a need for a new open-source OS to replace Linux, it would be used then. Once infrastructure becomes entrenched, the cost of dismantling or replacing it becomes enormous.

So you might argue:

'If AI is so great, shouldn't it be able to directly modify Linux's millions of lines of code right now?'

My answer is different:

'Why break something that already works? It only makes sense to change it when a problem actually arises.'

The example of Bun, originally written in Zig and later ported to Rust, illustrates this. Zig is a relatively new language, but whether for political reasons or not, Bun was eventually ported to Rust. And after the rewrite, Bun still works just fine.

And rewriting infrastructure from scratch is fundamentally a cost issue.

I can handle up to 60,000 lines of code on my own. With AI, I can handle up to around 200,000 lines. But building new infrastructure from scratch is an entirely different matter.

Why would you replace something that already works with AI? That's a separate question. If the current OS were no longer viable and a new one were needed, then the situation would be different.

In other words, I don't think your argument is wrong—I just don't think there's enough motivation for it.

In that sense, codebases that heavily use AI are already appearing in abundance.

There were issues with Open CLAW, but it was purely AI-written and still boasted a huge number of active users, right?

Same goes for Codex.

So my conclusion is this: AI is currently being used in layers above the infrastructure. But if a new infrastructure needs to be built, that's when AI will come into play.

In other words, it's a matter of motivation. Using AI for coding doesn't eliminate maintenance costs. And to be extreme, both maintenance and generation now require spending 'tokens'—you're paying money instead of the developer's time. We need to think about that cost.

In other words, there's no reason to break something that's already working.

I'd summarize it as: there's no reason to reinvent the wheel.

I have 3+ years of experience working on projects that integrate LLMs into the "old" approach to building software. Overall, whenever clients used LLM to analyse inputs without expecting them to be accurate, we were getting decent results. Not so much on the generative side, where LLMs are still producing crap output. This is on projects where humans wrote most of the code.

Things look way worse when working with vibed code. Over the last twelve months or so I encountered a number of issues with code and tests given to me by people with little or no coding experience claiming that this is a finished product and expecting me to "productionise it" (their words, not mine). Because they believe in LLMs like religious zealots and have no idea what programmers with actual experience of writing code are talking about there is a breakdown of communication and a lot of misunderstanding. On my latest project I was given a zip archive and asked to "make it work" by someone who calls themselves a "software architect" but has no idea how software development works. That person was surprised when we asked for a git repository, requirements, and design. None were given and we were told to use Claude to explain what the code is supposed to do. When we pressed for requirements the "architect" sent us a 4-page list of requirements based on the LLMs analysis of the contents of the zip file. It was so vague that it could apply to any project. Similarly, the architect vibed tickets in Jira and we had to clean them up as well, because of their vaugness and repetition or generic requirements. The three of us spent two months turning this turd into a piece of software with working tests and working implementation before we were told a PM will be assigned to our team and we will have to explain to him how the software works and what the requirements are. I am no longer on that project. I have had enough.

Another client forced addition on an AI PR reviewer. After initial excitement every dev on a 200+ team started ignoring it, because the fixes it suggests actually break code.

The marketing around LLMs convinced idiots that they are capable of producing software and that the greatest enemy of delivery are actual software developers with experience of delivering working software. The lowest point must be the recent series of ads I keep seeing on YouTube in which one character gets overly excited because he vibed a to do app... Every OS comes with one and if you don't like them, there are plenty of free and paid alternatives that cost less and work better than "your" vibed app.

I can't wait for the VC money to run out and the LLM madness to go to hell.

sentences.en: Which is also why it's so unbelievably useful for the ones for whom coding is the side career.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么它对于那些以编码为副业的人来说如此有用。

sentences.en: My main job is being a psychiatrist but i've always been coding in my free time and now my productivity gains are unfathomably high as they allow me to do things in days that would've taken me years of commute time.
sentences.zh: 我的主要工作是成为一名精神科医生，但我一直在空闲时间编写代码，现在我的生产力提高得难以想象，因为它们让我可以在几天内完成一些需要花费我多年通勤时间的事情。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's a live end.
sentences.zh: 有时候，这就是一个活生生的结局。

sentences.en: That's how they solved the Jacobian conjecture and found a lot of vulnerabilities.
sentences.zh: 他们就是这样解决了雅可比猜想并发现了很多漏洞。

sentences.en: I've been successfully using local LLMs for the past few months on equipment ranging from AMD 395+ strix halo, to dual nvidia gpus with 96GB ampere, to 24GB dual 3060, etc. They all produce text gen at almost readable rates.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几个月里，我在从 AMD 395+ strix halo 到具有 96GB 安培的双 nvidia gpus、到 24GB 双 3060 等设备上成功地使用了本地法学硕士。它们都以几乎可读的速率生成文本。

sentences.en: You can read the thinking traces, the editting of code in the opencode harness, etc.Along that same use, I've never touched any cloud service for code gen, and looked at docs or arena LLM.
sentences.zh: 你可以阅读思维轨迹、opencodeharness中的代码编辑等。沿着同样的用途，我从未接触过任何代码生成的云服务，并查看了文档或arena LLM。

sentences.en: From my POV, it seems like a lot of people arn't even paying attention to the LLMs output when they generate their projects.
sentences.zh: 从我的角度来看，似乎很多人在生成项目时甚至没有关注法学硕士的输出。

sentences.en: So I don't find it hard to believe there's seemingly intelligent people being swindled by LLMs, big or small, because they do make bizarre assumptions and go into code edits that don't make sense even when they appeared to be running.Then there's people that say they're in the ballpark of 500k context before they even get to work on something where these local models struggle when they get up to 100k both from generating and keeping scope on what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 因此，我不觉得很难相信有一些看似聪明的人被法学硕士（无论大小）欺骗，因为他们确实做出了奇怪的假设，并进行了即使在运行时也毫无意义的代码编辑。然后有人说，他们在开始工作之前就处于 500k 上下文的范围内，而这些本地模型在达到 100k 时就在生成和保持其范围方面陷入困境。做。

sentences.en: This is managed by opencode plugin dynamic-context-pruning that has the LLM rewrite sections of the context into summaries, while keeping the working context.
sentences.zh: 这是由 opencode 插件动态上下文修剪管理的，该插件使 LLM 将上下文的部分重写为摘要，同时保留工作上下文。

sentences.en: It works pretty wel where a session then gets into ~500k where the working increments from 30k-80k of useful life.So, I think we all underestimate how easily people can be swindled into poor development behaviors and _one_ reason, is the large cloud models just dump way more changes along a scope and can easily poison a whole chain of a feature or app implementation.So the OP above who got 3 months into an app they think is hitting a dead end is recognizable as having one idea in their head of what's being built and the LLM building something subtly different because they're inevitably only reviewing the things that confirm the specs in their head and don't look for the edge cases that break it.
sentences.zh: 当一个会话进入〜500k，其中工作增量从30k-80k的使用寿命开始时，它的效果非常好。所以，我认为我们都低估了人们多么容易被欺骗而陷入不良的开发行为，而_一个_原因是，大型云模型只是在一个范围内转储更多的变化，并且很容易毒害整个功能或应用程序实现链。因此，上面的OP在他们认为陷入死胡同的应用程序中投入了3个月的时间，可以被认为是他们脑子里对正在建造的东西有一个想法，而法学硕士建造的东西略有不同，因为他们不可避免地只会审查那些确认他们头脑中的规格的东西，而不是寻找破坏它的边缘情况。

sentences.en: That's a choice (unless your management thinks otherwise).
sentences.zh: 这是一个选择（除非你的管理层不这么认为）。

sentences.en: I don't need my agents running non stop.
sentences.zh: 我不需要我的特工不停地运转。

sentences.en: I tell them to start running once my walk is completed and I have a clear vision of what I want them to do.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他们在我完成步行后就开始跑步，并且我清楚地知道我希望他们做什么。

sentences.en: It seems to me this is the most reasonable approach.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是最合理的做法。

sentences.en: Using LLMs to remove the cognitive load from implementation details, scaffolding, and taking it from there to production grade code.
sentences.zh: 使用法学硕士消除实现细节、脚手架的认知负担，并将其从那里转化为生产级代码。

sentences.en: In short, like an IDE on steroids.I'm curious and hear a lot about agentic programming, yet hear little about the cognitive load from it.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，就像打了类固醇的 IDE。我很好奇，也听说过很多有关代理编程的知识，但很少听说它带来的认知负荷。

sentences.en: Having more code generated doesn't make you more productive, in fact, I would argue the contrary is the case.
sentences.zh: 生成更多代码并不会让你更有效率，事实上，我认为情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: There's more code to understand, more code to discard, an extra decision (which result do I pick?
sentences.zh: 有更多的代码需要理解，更多的代码需要丢弃，需要额外的决定（我选择哪个结果？

sentences.en: How do I split the workload through my agents), which is not at all how we operate (I.
sentences.zh: 我如何通过我的代理分配工作量），这根本不是我们的运作方式（I.

sentences.en: E context switching, limited by our cognitive energy, working task by task).I really don't buy the whole agentic thing.
sentences.zh: E 上下文切换，受我们的认知能量、工作任务的限制）。我真的不相信整个代理的事情。

sentences.en: The only reasonable use case I can see for it, is to scaffold multiple projects at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我能看到的唯一合理的用例是同时搭建多个项目。

sentences.en: This has happened to my side project too.
sentences.zh: 我的业余项目也发生过这种情况。

sentences.en: There's so much going on in the code now that I can't possibly grok it to make changes safely by myself any more.
sentences.zh: 现在代码中发生了太多事情，我不可能再自己安全地进行更改了。

sentences.en: But I think that's OK.
sentences.zh: 但我认为没关系。

sentences.en: Because I don't have to grok it anymore.I've been crafting beautiful code for almost 20 years - that itch is scratched.
sentences.zh: 因为我不再需要摸索它了。近 20 年来我一直在编写漂亮的代码 - 这种渴望得到了满足。

sentences.en: Now I just want to be productive and build cool stuff.
sentences.zh: 现在我只想提高工作效率并构建很酷的东西。

sentences.en: AI is helping me make a better end-product in a fraction of the time.
sentences.zh: 人工智能正在帮助我在很短的时间内制作出更好的最终产品。

sentences.en: As long as codex understands what's going on in the ball of spaghetti, there's no problem.
sentences.zh: 只要 Codex 能够理解意大利面条球中发生了什么，就没有问题。

sentences.en: Sure - if I was working in enterprise then this is no good.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果我在企业工作，那就不好了。

sentences.en: But for personal projects and small indie shops, it's fine.AI is just a new layer on top of the stack now.
sentences.zh: 但对于个人项目和小型独立商店来说，这很好。人工智能现在只是堆栈顶部的新层。

sentences.en: In the same way high-level languages are a layer on top of writing machine code manually.
sentences.zh: 同样，高级语言是手动编写机器代码之上的一层。

sentences.en: You just need to let go.
sentences.zh: 你只需要放手。

sentences.en: Anything built this way will have a hard limit on the ability to scale in terms of functionality and load.
sentences.zh: 以这种方式构建的任何东西都将在功能和负载方面的扩展能力受到严格限制。

sentences.en: Eventually it will get to a point where not even AI can work with it.It is hard to me to fathom why anyone would find those limits acceptable, especially with years of experience writing code.
sentences.zh: 最终，它会达到连人工智能都无法使用的地步。我很难理解为什么有人会认为这些限制是可以接受的，尤其是拥有多年编写代码经验的人。

sentences.en: It seems something like an experienced painter giving up on their art to doodle with crayons, and maybe that could be cathartic.
sentences.zh: 这看起来就像一位经验丰富的画家放弃了自己的艺术而用蜡笔涂鸦，也许这可以是一种宣泄。

sentences.en: Maybe you get experience with other aspects of your craft.
sentences.zh: 也许您会获得工艺其他方面的经验。

sentences.en: The ai does what you ask it to do.
sentences.zh: 人工智能会按照你的要求去做。

sentences.en: One thing you can ask is for it to refactor the code base to achieve some goal, for example to make new features easier to add , or to just make it more readable (though that’s a bad goal, no one agrees what is readable, and what AI finds readable may be different from what you think).I am saying this because I haven’t seen latest gen AI unable to implement something no matter how convoluted the code base.
sentences.zh: 你可以要求它重构代码库以实现某些目标，例如使新功能更容易添加，或者只是使其更具可读性（尽管这是一个糟糕的目标，没有人同意什么是可读的，AI认为可读的可能与你想象的不同）。我这么说是因为我还没有看到最新一代的AI无法实现某些东西，无论代码库多么复杂。

sentences.en: On the other hand, people easily get overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，人们很容易不知所措。

sentences.en: These days I have more faith in Claude implementing something for me than for a person, including me , doing it thoroughly enough on unfamiliar code bases (and for any big enough code base, large swathes of it will be unfamiliar to any individual developer).
sentences.zh: 这些天，我对 Claude 为我实现一些东西比为一个人（包括我）实现一些东西更有信心，在不熟悉的代码库上做得足够彻底（对于任何足够大的代码库，它的大部分内容对于任何个人开发人员来说都是不熟悉的）。

sentences.en: In order for you to properly guide it through a refactor, you have to understand the code, which becomes less possible as it grows into a mess of spaghetti.
sentences.zh: 为了让你正确地引导它完成重构，你必须理解代码，随着代码变得一团糟，这变得不太可能。

sentences.en: I think that's just setting yourself up for a massive amount of frustration.
sentences.zh: 我认为这只会让你自己陷入巨大的挫败感。

sentences.en: When there are multiple systems that need a refactor, each individual refactor becomes that much more complicated.
sentences.zh: 当有多个系统需要重构时，每个单独的重构都会变得更加复杂。

sentences.en: And trusting the tool that created the mess to sort it out seems a tad delusional.It's true that AI has an incredible ability to take in a massive amount of information and do useful work with it.
sentences.zh: 相信制造混乱的工具能够解决问题似乎有点痴心妄想。确实，人工智能具有令人难以置信的能力，可以吸收大量信息并利用这些信息进行有用的工作。

sentences.en: But it has no direct ability to exercise judgment, and with each iteration of reasoning and applied changes, its ability to hold the original intent degrades very differently from a human intelligence.
sentences.zh: 但它没有直接进行判断的能力，并且随着每次推理和应用变化的迭代，它保持原始意图的能力的下降与人类智能有很大不同。

sentences.en: We’ve already had those limits for years on any corporate project with average (or below) developers.I work with a lot of AI code, and it’s not any worse than what big teams were already producing.A small team of 2-3 really good humans is in a whole different league, but that has always been a very rare case. > In the same way high-level languages are a layer on top of writing machine code manually.Another layer, yes, but NOT "in the same way."
sentences.zh: 多年来，对于任何具有平均（或低于）开发人员的企业项目，我们都已经受到这些限制。我使用了大量的人工智能代码，这并不比大团队已经生产的代码更糟糕。一个由 2-3 名真正优秀的人组成的小团队处于一个完全不同的联盟，但这一直是一个非常罕见的情况。 > 以同样的方式，高级语言是手动编写机器代码之上的一层。另一层，是的，但不是“以相同的方式”。

sentences.en: It is a new, different kind of layer.
sentences.zh: 它是一个新的、不同类型的层。

sentences.en: The other layers were deterministic, not probabilistic.
sentences.zh: 其他层是确定性的，而不是概率性的。

sentences.en: Probabilistic algorithms are not new.
sentences.zh: 概率算法并不新鲜。

sentences.en: If the distribution is known you can bend surprisingly many things to your will in the long run - and the most interesting part is the long run can be unexpectedly short.LLMs are quite interesting in that regard because you have a lot of levers to influence the shape of the distribution; the ways are different for each model, so it’s a very experimental science, but applying the scientific method is exactly how you get good results.
sentences.zh: 如果分布是已知的，从长远来看，你可以让很多事情按照你的意愿进行调整——最有趣的是，长期来看可能会出乎意料地短暂。法学硕士在这方面非常有趣，因为你有很多杠杆可以影响分布的形状；每个模型的方法都不同，所以这是一门非常实验性的科学，但应用科学方法正是获得良好结果的方法。

sentences.en: The scientific method is not about running experiments and then trying to work out the gist of something.
sentences.zh: 科学方法不是进行实验然后试图找出某件事的要点。

sentences.en: It's about understanding and theory building and then doing experiments to verify your model.
sentences.zh: 这是关于理解和理论构建，然后进行实验来验证你的模型。

sentences.en: The end result is not an experimental result but a model that you understand and can use to build solutions etc. LLMs are bringing us back to pre- science correlations and superstitions.
sentences.zh: 最终结果不是实验结果，而是您可以理解并可以用来构建解决方案等的模型。法学硕士让我们回到了前科学的相关性和迷信。

sentences.en: That's why all the conversations on these threads about AI are so boring.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这些线程上有关人工智能的所有对话都如此无聊。

sentences.en: It's all anecdotes and tips and no understanding.
sentences.zh: 这都是轶事和技巧，没有任何理解。

sentences.en: I meant that no-one writes assembly anymore.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是没有人再写汇编了。

sentences.en: I wasn't around when that transition happened, but I bet there were the same "this high-level language is compiling to inefficient code, it's useless" comments.
sentences.zh: 当这种转变发生时，我不在场，但我敢打赌，一定会有同样的“这种高级语言正在编译成低效的代码，它毫无用处”的评论。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They know what you meant.
sentences.zh: 他们知道你的意思。

sentences.en: You missed the point of their response.A compiler is semantically deterministic.
sentences.zh: 你错过了他们的回应的要点。编译器在语义上是确定性的。

sentences.en: It has a spec.
sentences.zh: 它有一个规格。

sentences.en: Give it an input and you can know exactly what the output will do.
sentences.zh: 给它一个输入，你就可以确切地知道输出会做什么。

sentences.en: And if there's edge cases where behaviour is undefined, thats also well known apriori.(And yes, to get ahead of the nitpickers, I know the specific sequence of bytes the compiler will emit can vary (hence the difficulty of reproducible builds), hence why I said "semantically").LLMs do not share this property.
sentences.zh: 如果存在行为未定义的边缘情况，这也是众所周知的先验。（是的，为了领先于挑剔者，我知道编译器将发出的特定字节序列可能会有所不同（因此可重现构建的难度），因此我说“语义上”）。LLM 不共享此属性。

sentences.en: At all.
sentences.zh: 完全没有。

sentences.en: I mean not even closeThey are a completely new and different class of tool.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是根本就没有它们是一种全新的、不同类别的工具。

sentences.en: They are not just a step up the abstraction layer.
sentences.zh: 它们不仅仅是抽象层的一个台阶。

sentences.en: They're not compilers for English.
sentences.zh: 它们不是英语编译器。

sentences.en: To call them that is to fundamentally not grok what a compiler is or does.That doesn't make them bad.
sentences.zh: 这样称呼它们从根本上来说就是不了解编译器是什么或做什么。但这并不意味着它们很糟糕。

sentences.en: It just makes that analogy, and any conclusions you might draw from it, bad.
sentences.zh: 它只是让这个类比以及你从中得出的任何结论都是糟糕的。

sentences.en: Interesting point about "letting go".
sentences.zh: 关于“放手”的有趣观点。

sentences.en: I hear that quite a lot, which I find surprising.
sentences.zh: 我经常听到这样的说法，这让我感到惊讶。

sentences.en: In IT, when new technologies like cloud computing emerge people always need to adapt their workflows, and for some that is challenging e.g. going from manually maintained servers to virtual machines or containers that are just spun up and down on demand.
sentences.zh: 在 IT 领域，当云计算等新技术出现时，人们总是需要调整他们的工作流程，而对于某些人来说这是具有挑战性的，例如：从手动维护的服务器到按需启动和关闭的虚拟机或容器。

sentences.en: Maybe it is similar with AI, we gain new capabilities along one dimension like speed of development and we lose some capabilities along the way e.g. manual control of quality.
sentences.zh: 也许与人工智能类似，我们在一个维度上获得了新的能力，比如发展速度，同时我们也失去了一些能力，例如手动控制质量。

sentences.en: And of course there are large financial incentives here as well, maybe they are larger than we have ever seen before and the change also happens faster.
sentences.zh: 当然，这里也有大量的经济激励措施，也许它们比我们以前见过的更大，而且变化也发生得更快。

sentences.en: Cloud computing took probably multiple decades to be fully adopted (I think AWS became available in 2006 and we still see large corporations migrating to the cloud from their on premise setups today, though the adoption curve is flattening), LLMs have significantly higher adoption after only around 2-3 years of them becoming "production-ready".
sentences.zh: 云计算可能花了几十年的时间才被完全采用（我认为 AWS 于 2006 年推出，我们今天仍然看到大型公司从其本地设置迁移到云，尽管采用曲线正在趋于平坦），法学硕士在仅大约 2-3 年成为“生产就绪”后，其采用率就显着提高。

sentences.en: So naturally people struggle with how to adopt them and we need to figure out where they make sense and where not.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们很自然地会为如何采用它们而苦苦挣扎，我们需要弄清楚它们在哪里有意义，哪里没有意义。

sentences.en: That said it's precisely an engineers' job to figure that out, people that just see the upsides of this technology seem quite naive to me.I can see this struggle it in my organization as well, in the last year there was a big push to adopt AI everywhere and tons of initiatives to automate processes and produce code and text and other artefacts with LLMs.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，弄清楚这一点正是工程师的工作，那些只看到这项技术优点的人对我来说似乎相当天真。我也可以在我的组织中看到这种挣扎，去年，人们大力推动在各地采用人工智能，并采取了大量举措来自动化流程，并与法学硕士一起生产代码、文本和其他制品。

sentences.en: Now it seems the pendulum is swinging back a little as people see that all of the LLM generated stuff shows all of these subtle quality degradations, and people get tired of managing it as they are suddenly confronted with tons of additional information they need to manage.Given that models are still evolving and becoming better at a rapid pace I think that we will solve most of these issues in the near future, but for now I don't think the age of hand crafted code is over yet.I have been thinking about that machine code analogy before as well, I don't think it really holds.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们看到所有LLM生成的东西都显示出所有这些微妙的质量下降，人们厌倦了管理它，因为他们突然面临着需要管理的大量附加信息。鉴于模型仍在快速发展和变得更好，我认为我们将在不久的将来解决大部分这些问题，但目前我认为手工编写代码的时代还没有结束。我之前一直在思考机器代码类比好吧，我认为这并不成立。

sentences.en: Machine code is written in an automated way but following mostly deterministic rules that have been crafted through decades of manual optimizations and testing.
sentences.zh: 机器代码以自动化方式编写，但遵循通过数十年的手动优化和测试制定的大部分确定性规则。

sentences.en: AI generated code has nowhere near this level of scrutiny, testing and optimization behind itself.
sentences.zh: 人工智能生成的代码远没有经过如此程度的审查、测试和优化。

sentences.en: The fault rate of compilers and optimizers is incredibly small (I can't find any numbers but it must be on the order of ppm or ppb), AI generated code has fault rates that are even in the best case on the order of 99-99.99 % maybe (i.e. between one error per hundred lines and one error per ten thousand lines in the best case), try building anything complex using such a fault rate without manual correction and review.
sentences.zh: 编译器和优化器的错误率非常小（我找不到任何数字，但它必须在 ppm 或 ppb 的数量级），AI 生成的代码的错误率甚至在最好的情况下也可能在 99-99.99% 的数量级（即在最好的情况下在每百行 1 个错误到每万行 1 个错误之间），尝试使用这样的错误率构建任何复杂的东西，而无需手动纠正和审查。

sentences.en: It's impossible.
sentences.zh: 这是不可能的。

sentences.en: I have done it, I dabbled with writing a compiler, a database and even a simple web framework from first principles.
sentences.zh: 我已经做到了，我从第一原理开始涉足编写编译器、数据库，甚至是一个简单的 Web 框架。

sentences.en: I didn't get far, even though I had good mental models of these things and I carefully wrote RFCs and documents for the LLM, specified test cases etc...
sentences.zh: 尽管我对这些事情有很好的心理模型，并且我仔细地为 LLM 编写了 RFC 和文档、指定的测试用例等，但我并没有走得太远......

sentences.en: If you're lucky it will regurgitate some existing code or follow documented guidelines, but when you're on new territory these models won't be able to produce anything good.
sentences.zh: 如果你幸运的话，它会反省一些现有的代码或遵循记录的指南，但是当你进入新领域时，这些模型将无法产生任何好的结果。

sentences.en: I would really like to see a single example of someone vibe coding a high quality library or tool with LLMs, I haven't found anything and no one can point me to a complex codebase (say 10,000 lines or more) that was generated using high level prompts that looks decent and doesn't have multiple glaring issues that appear when looking at it in detail.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想看到有人用法学硕士编写高质量库或工具的一个例子，我没有找到任何东西，也没有人能给我指出一个复杂的代码库（比如 10,000 行或更多），它是使用高级提示生成的，看起来不错，并且在详细查看时没有出现多个明显的问题。

sentences.en: There's practical considerations with AI like it being a probabilistic layer and not deterministic in the way that compilers and deterministic, yes.But the "letting go" point is I think about what people enjoy.
sentences.zh: 人工智能有一些实际的考虑因素，比如它是一个概率层，而不是像编译器和确定性那样具有确定性，是的。但“放手”的一点是我认为人们喜欢什么。

sentences.en: Personally, I enjoy code.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我喜欢代码。

sentences.en: I've had jobs where I really enjoyed what I was doing because they gave me the opportunity to write interesting code.
sentences.zh: 我从事过一些我非常喜欢自己所做的工作，因为它们让我有机会编写有趣的代码。

sentences.en: The end product wasn't interesting to me.
sentences.zh: 最终产品对我来说并不有趣。

sentences.en: I had a great job building tools for companies that build a very popular consumer product that I've never owned or been interested in.
sentences.zh: 我在为公司开发工具方面做得很好，这些公司开发了一种我从未拥有过或不感兴趣的非常受欢迎的消费产品。

sentences.en: So the software we were building to assist in creating those products wasn't interesting to me in terms of what it is, but the job was motivating and interesting because of the technical problems I got to solve.I think that's one of the big divides we're seeing in comments now.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们为帮助创建这些产品而构建的软件本身对我来说并不有趣，但由于我必须解决技术问题，这项工作充满激励性且有趣。我认为这是我们现在在评论中看到的最大分歧之一。

sentences.en: There are people who want to build things for the sake of the final product.
sentences.zh: 有些人想要为了最终产品而构建东西。

sentences.en: They're happy because LLMs speed that up by a lot, at least initially.
sentences.zh: 他们很高兴，因为法学硕士大大加快了这一速度，至少在最初是这样。

sentences.en: Then there are people who enjoy the process and craft of writing code.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人喜欢编写代码的过程和技巧。

sentences.en: For them it's hard to let go of manual coding because that's the enjoyable part of the work. > They're happy because LLMs speed that up by a lot, at least initially.
sentences.zh: 对于他们来说，很难放弃手动编码，因为这是工作中令人愉快的部分。 > 他们很高兴，因为法学硕士大大加快了这一速度，至少在最初是这样。

sentences.en: Then there are people who enjoy the process and craft of writing code.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人喜欢编写代码的过程和技巧。

sentences.en: For them it's hard to let go of manual coding because that's the enjoyable part of the work.
sentences.zh: 对于他们来说，很难放弃手动编码，因为这是工作中令人愉快的部分。

sentences.en: coding enjoyer here, but for me i want it to be an assistant to speed up what im doing (in the "bicycle for the mind" kind of way) or a problem solver for when i got really stuck; i feel like "agentic" workflows miss a lot of this cause its like talking to someone through slack...
sentences.zh: 在这里编码享受者，但对我来说，我希望它成为一个助手，以加快我正在做的事情（以“思维自行车”的方式），或者当我真正陷入困境时，它是一个问题解决者；我觉得“代理”工作流程错过了很多这样的事情，因为它就像通过松弛与某人交谈......

sentences.en: thats not enjoyable and also too far removed from the actual code/problem im working on; i think there is an opportunity for much better ux here...
sentences.zh: 这并不令人愉快，而且与我正在处理的实际代码/问题相距太远；我认为这里有机会获得更好的用户体验......

sentences.en: The real value I think never really was the code, it was the learnings from the journey to get to the code.
sentences.zh: 我认为真正的价值从来都不是代码，而是从编写代码的过程中学到的东西。

sentences.en: The struggle allowed for iterative discovery of the real requirements and technical challenges.
sentences.zh: 这场斗争允许迭代地发现真正的需求和技术挑战。

sentences.en: With AI you skip that path and it looks like you've achieved your goal only on a superficial level.I think this doesn't mean AI is useless (it's not), it's just that we have to think harder about the requirements and end-stage verification and have less trust in the process to result into valuable outcome.
sentences.zh: 有了人工智能，你就跳过了这条路，看起来你只是在表面上实现了你的目标。我认为这并不意味着人工智能是无用的（事实并非如此），只是我们必须更加仔细地考虑需求和最终阶段的验证，并且对产生有价值结果的过程缺乏信任。

sentences.en: I’ve found it very useful to leverage the “speed” of AI to iron out all of the UX-questions of a greenfield side project (an organiser for a/my family).My first aim is to get to what feels like v1 feature-completeness.
sentences.zh: 我发现利用人工智能的“速度”来解决绿地项目（一个/我的家庭的组织者）的所有用户体验问题非常有用。我的第一个目标是达到 v1 功能完整性。

sentences.en: My approach is building out the feature, dogfooding it for a few days, work out the bits I don’t like, adjusting, and then rinse and repeating.I don’t like the finer UI details (the colours it’s chosen for instance), nor do I fully jive with how it’s implemented the business logic (it’s verbose and needlessly fancy in some places) but - that’s not what I’m concerned about now.
sentences.zh: 我的方法是构建该功能，对其进行几天的测试，找出我不喜欢的部分，进行调整，然后冲洗并重复。我不喜欢更精细的 UI 细节（例如它选择的颜色），也不完全同意它如何实现业务逻辑（它在某些地方很冗长且不必要的花哨），但是 - 这不是我现在关心的。

sentences.en: I’m concerned about whether my wife and I find the tool useful.
sentences.zh: 我担心我和我的妻子是否觉得这个工具有用。

sentences.en: (We do, huzzah).I’m now looking forward to sitting down and redesigning the finer details of the UI to my taste, and then, having established pretty solidly how the backend is going to need to work, how I would do it, and then crack on and do a rewrite from the ground up so that I can maintain/extend it more effectively going forward.Which is all to say, I find Claude and it’s kin are excellent for prototyping (answering questions, giving someone something to play with), and for uncovering/discovering the requirements of a project which make it then easier to do “properly” if you feel it hasn’t done a good job already.Everyone will have their own approach of course, but I’ve found it helpful to take this one in this case.
sentences.zh: （我们确实这么做了，huzzah）。我现在期待着坐下来，根据我的口味重新设计 UI 的细节，然后，非常扎实地确定后端需要如何工作，我将如何做，然后从头开始进行重写，以便我可以更有效地维护/扩展它。总而言之，我发现 Claude 和它的亲戚非常适合原型设计（回答问题，给别人提供帮助）一些可以玩的东西），以及揭示/发现项目的需求，如果你觉得项目还没有做得很好，那么可以更容易地“正确”地做。当然，每个人都会有自己的方法，但我发现在这种情况下采取这种方法很有帮助。

sentences.en: For my projects, I can produce with LLMs a codebase that I'd be proud of, but it requires extensive use of the plan mode and nagging anytime the implementation looks much more complex than the feature at hand requires.Anytime I tried spec driven development, it produced total garbage, the problem is that the model usually swings too far, if they write unnecessary complexity, a nag about it and you risk it code golfing, this problem across 100 lines of specs and you're guaranteed it will swing too far on some segments you just wanted X slightly more than Y (usually for me it was reliability dropped for better readability since # users = # developers = 1)Another thing I dropped is steering implementation design too early, start with the goal and nag in the direction you want, it works well for me but might not work well for big complex codebases.For now I love LLM coding but I'm sure my opinion will change if I have to review code from a developer that does the 1 prompt = 1 PR without looking at the code jutsu.
sentences.zh: 对于我的项目，我可以用 LLM 生成一个令我感到自豪的代码库，但它需要广泛使用计划模式，并且在实现看起来比手头的功能所需的复杂得多的任何时候都需要唠叨。每当我尝试规范驱动开发时，它都会产生完全垃圾，问题是模型通常会摆动得太远，如果他们写了不必要的复杂性，对它的唠叨和你冒着代码打高尔夫球的风险，这个问题跨越 100 行规范，并且你保证它在某些部分会摆动得太远你只是想要 X 比 Y 稍多一点（通常对我来说，为了更好的可读性，可靠性下降了，因为 # 用户 = # 开发人员 = 1）我放弃的另一件事是过早地指导实现设计，从目标开始，然后朝着你想要的方向唠叨，它对我来说效果很好，但对于大型复杂的代码库可能效果不好。现在我喜欢 LLM 编码，但我确信，如果我必须审查来自开发人员的代码，该开发人员在不查看代码柔术的情况下执行 1 提示 = 1 PR，我的观点会改变。

sentences.en: I've found that "build X with framework Y" produces better results than "build X".
sentences.zh: 我发现“使用框架 Y 构建 X”比“构建 X”产生更好的结果。

sentences.en: Possibly because many architectural decisions have already been made by the framework authors.Before you throw away, I propose having an LLM write a comprehensive spec from your code, then a clean-room implementation.
sentences.zh: 可能是因为框架作者已经做出了许多架构决策。在您放弃之前，我建议让法学硕士根据您的代码编写全面的规范，然后进行干净的实现。

sentences.en: It's an interesting experiment, if nothing else.
sentences.zh: 如果没有别的的话，这是一个有趣的实验。

sentences.en: It’s a garbage collection problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个垃圾收集问题。

sentences.en: They’re good at adding stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们擅长添加东西。

sentences.en: They’re bad at removing stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们不擅长删除东西。

sentences.en: You have to go out of your way to have them remove stuff; rubrics, byte for byte identical outputs, bug for bug compatibility etc and then convince the cursed things that it’s still safe to rip and replace.
sentences.zh: 你必须想尽办法让他们把东西拿走；标题、逐字节相同的输出、错误兼容性等错误，然后让那些被诅咒的东西相信它仍然可以安全地删除和替换。

sentences.en: Bonus points when you get them to stop before the ‘replace’ and everything still works.
sentences.zh: 当你让它们在“替换”之前停止并且一切仍然有效时，可以获得奖励积分。

sentences.en: When you're in the trenches actually making code changes yourself, you get irritated and are driven towards improving the code as you implement new features.
sentences.zh: 当您亲自亲自更改代码时，您会感到恼火，并在实现新功能时被迫改进代码。

sentences.en: AI never does because it never has to.
sentences.zh: 人工智能从来不会这样做，因为它从来没有必要这样做。

sentences.en: And because you're not in the trenches, you don't actually experience the frustration of managing the code base.
sentences.zh: 而且因为您不在第一线，所以您实际上不会经历管理代码库的挫败感。

sentences.en: So from your tactical view everything is fine, and when you're reviewing an isolated change you don't have the context of everything the AI had to read and figure out to get there.
sentences.zh: 因此，从你的战术角度来看，一切都很好，当你审查一个孤立的变更时，你没有人工智能必须阅读和弄清楚才能到达那里的所有内容的背景。

sentences.en: If you had to wade through shit to figure out how to implement something, you'd have made those refactors a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 如果你必须费尽心思才能弄清楚如何实现某些东西，那么你很久以前就已经进行了这些重构。

sentences.en: AI just eats it up and serves you a new plate of slop.
sentences.zh: 人工智能只是把它吃掉，然后为你提供一盘新的泔水。

sentences.en: It's a blessing and a curse depending on who you ask.AIs greatest strength is still throwaway code.
sentences.zh: 这是福还是祸取决于你问的是谁。人工智能的最大优势仍然是一次性代码。

sentences.en: It cannot write some kind of short texts either.The experiment was: given existing Experience section of Senior Software Engineer CV (manually and carefully written), write 2-4 lines of high pitch About [me].gpt-sol-xhigh just could not do it, making a complete AI slop mess.It became substantially better when I asked to get a sample of real Senior/Principal engineers CVs, that it would be able to connect with meaningful online presence/contributions of their authors, and draw ideas from that.Nevertheless, the remaining issues were critical, with their classes spanning:- word for word repetition;- tautology (phrases mapping to the same semantic entity);- category mistakes (combining apples with oranges);- faulty composition of generalised and concrete terms.Before throwing it away I decided to give it a try and asked for strict prompt following, setting low logical errors threshold, and eventually providing a formal proof that it complied.It took spaCy, doing NER and dependency parsing; then I suggested adding stanza for constituency parsing.After slapping together the artefacts of analysis and thinking a bit, it produced great phrase (to my taste).-Then when I asked to apply the framework and improve bullet points in some experience block, it did 2 of 4 well, then miserably broke down; I’m not sure if it’s harness issue (codex) or fundamental model restriction.-So no, without substantial investment in steering, SOTA AI doesn’t perform even remotely close to a human, in complex reasoning.
sentences.zh: 它也不能写某种短文本。实验是：给定高级软件工程师简历的现有经验部分（手动且仔细地编写），写 2-4 行高调的 About [me].gpt-sol-xhigh 就是做不到，使 AI 变得一团糟。当我要求获取真实的高级/首席工程师简历样本时，它变得更好，它将能够与作者有意义的在线存在/贡献联系起来，并汲取想法尽管如此，剩下的问题仍然很关键，它们的类别涵盖：-逐字重复；-同义反复（短语映射到同一语义实体）；-类别错误（将苹果与橙子组合）；-广义和具体术语的错误组合。在扔掉它之前，我决定尝试一下，并要求严格的提示遵循，设置较低的逻辑错误阈值，并最终提供它符合要求的正式证明。它需要 spaCy，进行 NER 和依赖项解析；然后我建议添加用于选区解析的节。在将分析和思考的产物放在一起之后，它产生了很棒的短语（符合我的口味）。-然后当我要求应用框架并改进某些经验块中的要点时，它在 4 中做得很好，然后就崩溃了；我不确定这是线束问题（codex）还是基本模型限制。-所以不，如果没有在转向方面进行大量投资，SOTA AI 在复杂推理方面的表现甚至无法接近人类。

sentences.en: It's funny, because right now the top news on HN is about OpenAI's "Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science".So I suppose which is it?
sentences.zh: 很有趣，因为现在 HN 上的头条新闻是关于 OpenAI 的“数学和理论计算机科学的十大进展”。所以我想是哪一个？

sentences.en: Is AI going to replace us all, or it's not even capable of writing basic code?I've never seen a topic so divisive where people's experiences differ in such magnitudes.I suppose the biggest thing drawing this distinction is that on one side, you have AI releasing features which is all the business cares about.
sentences.zh: 人工智能会取代我们所有人，还是它甚至无法编写基本代码？我从未见过一个如此分裂的话题，人们的经历差异如此之大。我认为造成这种区别的最大原因是，一方面，你拥有人工智能发布的功能，这是所有企业关心的。

sentences.en: On the other side you have it generating slop, which is all engineering ever cares about.I think in this battle, executives are going to eventually win.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，它会产生污水，这是所有工程人员关心的问题。我认为在这场战斗中，高管们最终会获胜。

sentences.en: They had been looking for a way to crush the engineering department's value for years and AI seems to be their golden ticket.The pesky dev cost center can finally shrink and they don't have to bother paying them six figures thanks to LLMs..
sentences.zh: 多年来，他们一直在寻找一种方法来压垮工程部门的价值，而人工智能似乎是他们的金票。令人讨厌的开发成本中心终于可以缩小，多亏了法学硕士，他们不必费心向他们支付六位数的费用。

sentences.en: The exact opposite has happened for me.
sentences.zh: 我的情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: I used to review every pr, give read only access to db.
sentences.zh: 我曾经审查每个公关，授予对数据库的只读访问权限。

sentences.en: Now with codex 5.6 sol high I let it rip.
sentences.zh: 现在，随着 Codex 5.6 sol 高，我让它撕裂。

sentences.en: I do sometimes quickly scan the pr but mostly I've been regulated to a manual tester.
sentences.zh: 我有时会快速浏览公关，但大多数情况下我都被限制为手动测试人员。

sentences.en: Run the feature, check the DB, verify the UI.
sentences.zh: 运行该功能，检查数据库，验证用户界面。

sentences.en: Build unit and E2E around everything.
sentences.zh: 围绕一切构建单元和 E2E。

sentences.en: Mind you I am not working with production data yet.My stack for this project is React Native and Supabase which I've got a good amount of experience using.Which LLM are you using? > but when running multiple "Please look for issues" iterations it would never have spotted the issue by itself.Nah that's old meta, you're supposed to generate candidate issues with an agent swarm running at high temperature.
sentences.zh: 请注意，我还没有处理生产数据。这个项目的堆栈是 React Native 和 Supabase，我有丰富的使用经验。您使用的是哪个 LLM？ > 但是当运行多个“请查找问题”迭代时，它本身永远不会发现问题。不，这是旧元，您应该通过在高温下运行的代理群来生成候选问题。

sentences.en: It's the only way to fly!
sentences.zh: 这是唯一的飞翔方式！

sentences.en: In my experience AI doesn't create the same abstractions as a human developer and you see this very quickly on a complex code base if you let the AI run wild.Humans, and especially good developers, naturally create really good mental models for how to think about complex systems.
sentences.zh: 根据我的经验，人工智能不会创建与人类开发人员相同的抽象，如果你让人工智能疯狂运行，你很快就会在复杂的代码库上看到这一点。人类，尤其是优秀的开发人员，自然会创建非常好的思维模型来思考复杂的系统。

sentences.en: We have to.
sentences.zh: 我们必须。

sentences.en: That's ultimately how we build complex systems.Refactoring (when it's not simply upgrading packages or changing languages) typically happens because we realise there's a better way to model the system we're building and we want our code to reflect the model in our minds.AIs today simply don't do this.
sentences.zh: 这最终就是我们构建复杂系统的方式。重构（当它不仅仅是升级软件包或更改语言时）通常会发生，因为我们意识到有更好的方法来对我们正在构建的系统进行建模，并且我们希望我们的代码能够反映我们头脑中的模型。今天的人工智能根本不这样做。

sentences.en: They write code that solves a specific problem, and while they do this well, they don't seem to create well defined and well reasoned models about how to think about complex systems.
sentences.zh: 他们编写解决特定问题的代码，虽然他们做得很好，但他们似乎没有创建明确定义和合理推理的模型来思考如何思考复杂系统。

sentences.en: Or maybe they do, but the AI definitely doesn't say, "hey, I think what you're building is more like x than y, so I want to spend 20 minutes of refactoring your codebase".I guess to use an analogy, imagine trying to tell someone how to build a bike who has never heard of a bike before, and therefore has no mental model of what a bike is.
sentences.zh: 或者也许他们会这样做，但人工智能绝对不会说，“嘿，我认为你正在构建的东西更像是 x 而不是 y，所以我想花 20 分钟重构你的代码库”。我想用一个类比，想象一下试图告诉一个以前从未听说过自行车的人如何制造一辆自行车，因此对自行车是什么没有任何心理模型。

sentences.en: You'd probably start by telling them to put two wheels on a frame, then to add a seat on top, then to a add some pedals and attachment them to the wheel with a chain...
sentences.zh: 您可能会首先告诉他们将两个轮子放在框架上，然后在顶部添加一个座椅，然后添加一些踏板并用链条将它们连接到轮子上......

sentences.en: At the end of this process that person might create something bike-like, and it might kinda do the thing you want, but it would likely be very different from the bike someone would build if they had a very clear mental model of what a bike is.I suspect this is why current AIs rapidly hit a limit after the prototyping stage.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程结束时，人们可能会创造出类似自行车的东西，它可能会做你想要的事情，但如果他们对自行车有一个非常清晰的心智模型，它可能会与某人建造的自行车有很大不同。我怀疑这就是为什么当前的人工智能在原型设计阶段后迅速达到极限。

sentences.en: I don't think task duration is the right way to think about this limitation.
sentences.zh: 我认为任务持续时间不是考虑此限制的正确方法。

sentences.en: I suspect it's more of a proxy for how complex a task can become before the AI isn't able to create a deep enough model of the problem it's trying to solve, so begins to hit complexity limits and just spits out spaghetti code.AIs are getting better quick though.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑它更多地代表了在人工智能无法为它试图解决的问题创建足够深入的模型之前任务会变得多么复杂，因此开始达到复杂性限制并只是吐出意大利面条代码。不过，人工智能正在变得越来越快。

sentences.en: I think they'll get there soon, but people are creating a lot of mess in their codebases in the mean time.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们很快就会实现这一目标，但与此同时人们在他们的代码库中造成了很多混乱。

sentences.en: I don't have the same experience at work.After two years of investment LLMs can write code mostly on their own due to a combination of proper architecture (you can't really "cheat it"), documentation, instructions and human checks.On my personal projects, it's still a super good match for building prototypes, but at some point if you don't write it your own you lose the plot.
sentences.zh: 我在工作中没有相同的经验。经过两年的投资，法学硕士可以大部分自己编写代码，因为适当的架构（你不能真正“欺骗它”）、文档、说明和人工检查的结合。在我的个人项目中，它仍然是构建原型的超级匹配，但在某些时候，如果你不自己编写它，你就会失去情节。

sentences.en: So you're bound to write it your own before handing it off to LLMs.In any case there are no black or white solutions, and there are aspects that make me think that the more capable the less fit it is for serious projects at some point.
sentences.zh: 因此，在将其交给法学硕士之前，您必须自己编写它。无论如何，没有非黑即白的解决方案，并且有些方面让我认为能力越强，在某些时候就越不适合严肃的项目。

sentences.en: This mirrors my experience too, long term use starts showing incoherence that is impossible to see in isolation.The funny thing with LLM’s is that with a sufficient sized code base they pretty much will loop forever if you tell them to find and fix issues, making new ones as they fix old ones.
sentences.zh: 这也反映了我的经验，长期使用开始表现出不连贯性，这是不可能单独看到的。LLM的有趣之处在于，如果你告诉他们发现并修复问题，在修复旧问题的同时产生新问题，那么如果你告诉他们发现并修复问题，他们几乎会永远循环，如果你有足够大的代码库，他们几乎会永远循环。

sentences.en: There’s an infinite number of ”working stuff” implementations, which is kind of the problem, bad decisions multiply.
sentences.zh: 有无限数量的“工作内容”实现，这就是问题所在，错误的决策会成倍增加。

sentences.en: That said, looking at small parts of code for improvements tend to work very well for me, optimizing things like data structures, iterations and SQL queries.I just hope my bank doesn’t go Claude code all the way any time soon.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，查看一小部分代码进行改进对我来说往往非常有效，可以优化数据结构、迭代和 SQL 查询等内容。我只是希望我的银行不会很快就完全采用 Claude 代码。

sentences.en: It's hard to take criticism like this seriously when you didn't say the model you used.
sentences.zh: 当你没有说出你使用的模型时，很难认真对待这样的批评。

sentences.en: It's like someone complaining about a car's performance but they leave out the brand and year.
sentences.zh: 这就像有人抱怨汽车的性能，但他们忽略了品牌和年份。

sentences.en: If you don't think that's relevant I just can't take you seriously.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为这无关紧要，我就无法认真对待你。

sentences.en: it's hard to take this stock dismissal seriously when it's been repeated ad nauseum, for years, every time a new generation is released.
sentences.zh: 多年来，每次新一代产品发布时，这种股票被解雇的情况都会令人作呕地重复出现，因此很难认真对待这种情况。

sentences.en: What's the point?
sentences.zh: 有什么意义？

sentences.en: It doesn't matter what model he says, he'll either get "that model is bad" or "you're holding it wrong".I've used 5.6 Sol on 1M context and max thinking, and also Opus 5 on max context and thinking, and I agree with that comment.
sentences.zh: 不管他说什么模型，他要么得到“那个模型不好”，要么得到“你的观点是错误的”。我在 1M 上下文和最大思维上使用了 5.6 Sol，在最大上下文和思维上也使用了 Opus 5，我同意这个评论。

sentences.en: Now what?
sentences.zh: 现在怎么办？

sentences.en: Does this information matter or will you just say we must be doing something wrong?
sentences.zh: 这些信息重要吗？或者您只是说我们一定做错了什么？

sentences.en: There seem to be some people who just want to believe that AI can currently replace human developers (in the future, sure - the CEO will be AI too), despite there being no logical reason to believe this if you are at all aware of the data-driven nature of LLMs.The AI we have today consists of a generic base model whose software expertise comes from specific training designed to impart specific skills.
sentences.zh: 似乎有些人只是想相信人工智能目前可以取代人类开发人员（当然，将来 - 首席执行官也将是人工智能），尽管如果你完全意识到法学硕士的数据驱动性质，就没有逻辑理由相信这一点。我们今天拥有的人工智能由一个通用基础模型组成，其软件专业知识来自旨在传授特定技能的特定培训。

sentences.en: We don't have AGI - we have a collection of narrow skills that kinda looks like general until you start poking it.The core software skill today's AI has is coding, which is the low hanging fruit.
sentences.zh: 我们没有通用人工智能——我们有一系列狭隘的技能，在你开始探索之前，这些技能看起来有点通用。当今人工智能的核心软件技能是编码，这是唾手可得的成果。

sentences.en: There is tons of code available to train on, and RLVR for coding is easy - does the code compile and work as intended.There is also plenty of training data available for some of the other skills you may want the AI to have.For example, if you want the AI to have some human taste in designing web pages, then there is plenty of training data for that, and it's easy to hire humans to do A/B testing and express their preferences.You want to the AI to be an expert hacker like Mythos?
sentences.zh: 有大量的代码可供训练，RLVR 的编码很容易 - 代码是否按预期编译和工作。还有大量的训练数据可用于您可能希望 AI 具备的其他一些技能。例如，如果您希望 AI 在设计网页方面具有人类的品味，那么有大量的训练数据，并且很容易雇用人类进行 A/B 测试并表达他们的偏好。您希望 AI 成为像 Mythos 这样的专家黑客吗？

sentences.en: Just put it in a playground where it can build and test it's exploits and let it learn from that via RL - no problem since it's generating it's own training data.So, for some of the "collection of narrow skills", such as coding, that you want your wannabe-developer AI to have, training data is no problem.
sentences.zh: 只需将它放在一个游乐场中，它可以构建和测试它的漏洞，并让它通过 RL 从中学习 - 没问题，因为它生成自己的训练数据。因此，对于一些“狭隘技能的集合”，例如编码，你希望你的想要成为开发者的人工智能拥有，训练数据是没有问题的。

sentences.en: Where it IS a problem is for architecture/design and reasoning about large systems, since:a) The majority of larger systems, where architecture and design starts to be an issue, are private commercial software.
sentences.zh: 问题在于大型系统的架构/设计和推理，因为：a）大多数大型系统（其中架构和设计开始成为问题）都是私有商业软件。

sentences.en: Training documentation is not available.b) Even for open source projects, designers just don't tend to blog their thought processes - they just silently apply their expertise, and even where design documents exist they tend to document what was produced not WHY (the reasoning data that might let an AI learn to design itself).c) A lot of the value of good architecture/design is not just about taking user/business requirements (or the vibe coders' request!)
sentences.zh: 培训文档不可用。b) 即使对于开源项目，设计师也不倾向于在博客中记录他们的思维过程 - 他们只是默默地应用他们的专业知识，即使存在设计文档，他们也倾向于记录生成的内容而不是原因（可能让 AI 学会自行设计的推理数据）。c) 良好架构/设计的很多价值不仅仅在于满足用户/业务需求（或氛围编码员的要求！）

sentences.en: and mapping that into something that works, but rather about understanding the future consequences of design decisions - there will always be many ways of doing something, so what criteria do you use to pick one over the other?
sentences.zh: 并将其映射为可行的东西，而是了解设计决策的未来后果 - 做某事总是有多种方法，那么您使用什么标准来选择一种方法呢？

sentences.en: Which choices will be easy to debug both in development and production, which will be easy to modify for anticipated future requirements, etc. These also tend to be things that are not documented - no training data available - but are rather just the accumulated expertise of the battle-hardened developer.Of course, an LLM will have a go at anything, but if you want an AI to be a human-equivalent developer, not just a coder, then you need more than just training data for coding - you need training data for each of the individual developer skills you want the AI to have, and training data for some of these, such as for reasoning-based design/architecture is in extremely limited supply.
sentences.zh: 哪些选择在开发和生产中都很容易调试，哪些选择很容易根据预期的未来需求进行修改，等等。这些也往往是没有记录的东西——没有可用的培训数据——而只是久经沙场的开发人员积累的专业知识。当然，法学硕士可以尝试任何事情，但如果你希望人工智能成为相当于人类的开发人员，而不仅仅是编码员，那么你需要的不仅仅是用于编码的训练数据——你需要针对你想要的每种开发人员技能的训练数据。人工智能以及其中一些的训练数据（例如基于推理的设计/架构）的供应极其有限。

sentences.en: LLMs can write excellent code a few thousand lines at a time but they absolutely can't create a cohesive million line codebase.
sentences.zh: LLM 可以一次编写几千行的优秀代码，但他们绝对无法创建一个有凝聚力的百万行代码库。

sentences.en: I had a funny yet tragic experience about LLM last weekA CICD flow had broken.
sentences.zh: 上周我对 LLM 经历了一次有趣而又悲惨的经历，CICD 流程中断了。

sentences.en: It was not giving the URL of a deployed service.A team member used AI to fix it without reading the code and AI added 55 lines of codeWhen I noticed the issue, I modified the code by removing 5 extra lines and used the right command to get the urlEarlier I was doing a grep and matching the output against .com to get the url Recently I noticed that the utility provided a --format json option that was much cleaner! > but looking at the whole picture everything is subtly wrong in multiple ways.That would also make a great description for human societies, wouldn't it?Actually, after second thought, actually LLMs at least give the surface level impression, which might not be exactly the case for humanity at the moment.Ok, sarcasm apart, I'm fine with LLM at the moment as a technology.
sentences.zh: 它没有给出已部署服务的 URL。团队成员使用 AI 来修复它，而无需阅读代码，AI 添加了 55 行代码当我注意到这个问题时，我通过删除 5 行额外的代码来修改代码，并使用正确的命令来获取 url 之前我正在执行 grep 并将输出与 .com 进行匹配以获取 url 最近我注意到该实用程序提供了一个更干净的 --format json 选项！ > 但从整体来看，一切都在多个方面出现了微妙的错误。这对人类社会也有很好的描述，不是吗？实际上，经过再三思考，实际上法学硕士至少给人一种表面的印象，而目前人类的情况可能并不完全如此。好吧，除了讽刺之外，我目前对法学硕士作为一项技术感到满意。

sentences.en: How we use it, what impact it has on society is certainly more of a concern than the technology itself.
sentences.zh: 我们如何使用它，它对社会产生什么影响，肯定比技术本身更值得关注。

sentences.en: Compared to weapons, at least they're not fundamentally designed specifically to harm and threat.
sentences.zh: 与武器相比，至少它们从根本上来说并不是专门为伤害和威胁而设计的。

sentences.en: Why is the answer of LLM-maximalists always you are holding it wrong?I think a lot of experienced programmers, who have adopted LLMs early on, have the same finding: yes, LLMs give a great productivity boost.
sentences.zh: 为什么LLM-最大化主义者的答案总是你认为是错误的？我认为很多早期采用LLM的经验丰富的程序员都有相同的发现：是的，LLM可以极大地提高生产力。

sentences.en: No, you cannot let agents completely wild without plenty of human supervision, because it will lead to a big ball of mud and atrophy knowledge of humans.
sentences.zh: 不，你不能在没有大量人类监督的情况下让智能体完全疯狂，因为这会导致人类知识的一大泥球和萎缩。

sentences.en: I think these are relevant data points and they should be taken into account during the adoption of LLMs.This type of LLM-maximalist thinking is thoroughly anti-scientific, they want to throw away data points that are not in line with the hypothesis they want to see confirmed at all cost.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些都是相关的数据点，在采用法学硕士的过程中应该考虑到它们。这种类型的法学硕士极端主义思维是彻底反科学的，他们想扔掉那些不符合他们希望不惜一切代价得到证实的假设的数据点。

sentences.en: look at the sibling reply.
sentences.zh: 看看兄弟的回复。

sentences.en: these back-handed concessions are always either “AI is a great productivity boost if you’re just slamming out a CRUD web app” or the special snowflake “my big beautiful codebase is too complex.”
sentences.zh: 这些反手让步总是要么“如果你只是猛烈抨击 CRUD Web 应用程序，人工智能会极大地提高生产力”，要么是特殊的雪花“我的大而美丽的代码库太复杂了。”

sentences.en: maybe they are holding it, wrong with attitudes like that it’s hard to take them seriously.
sentences.zh: 也许他们持有这种态度，这样的态度是错误的，很难认真对待他们。

sentences.en: the phd holders at my office are some of the most prodigious vibe coders we haveps: since when was complexity ever a good defense for why your codebase is difficult to work in?
sentences.zh: 我办公室的博士学位持有者是我们拥有的最出色的编码员：从什么时候开始，复杂性成为了为什么你的代码库难以使用的良好辩护？

sentences.en: It's not even complexity; raw size suffices to make a codebase hard for the LLM to manage, which is especially bad given the high ratio of LLM lines to ideal lines for any given change.
sentences.zh: 这甚至不是复杂性；而是复杂性。原始大小足以使 LLM 难以管理代码库，考虑到对于任何给定更改，LLM 行与理想行的比率很高，这尤其糟糕。

sentences.en: E.g., if a concurrent hashmap is a reasonable primitive, it won't check if any of the existing ones are good fits.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果并发哈希图是一个合理的原语，它不会检查现有的哈希图是否适合。

sentences.en: It'll instead prefer to implement something simpler but totally broken, or else it'll try and fail to build yet another concurrent hashmap.
sentences.zh: 相反，它会更喜欢实现一些更简单但完全损坏的东西，否则它将尝试构建另一个并发哈希图，但会失败。

sentences.en: If you fix that by giving it explicit instructions to use a particular implementation, it'll manufacture extra (incorrect or low-performance) methods out of nowhere rather than solving within the constraints of the existing API -- think things like adding a global lock around the whole thing to make "concurrent" iteration possible when iteration isn't even a primitive the thing you asked the LLM to do requires.A colleague of mine had the observation that the problem we're seeing is a strong tendency to produce solutions which add extra, undesirable connections in the code, resulting in inordinately complex API boundaries which are hard to properly disentangle.That's all fixable with enough effort, but it's hard to ignore that experience when somebody comes along and tells you that vibe coding really does suffice by itself, and you can just point a good model and harness at a ticket and a codebase and let it rip.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过给它明确的指令来使用特定的实现来解决这个问题，它会凭空制造出额外的（不正确或低性能）方法，而不是在现有 API 的约束下解决问题——想想像在整个事情上添加一个全局锁，以便在迭代甚至不是你要求 LLM 做的事情所需的原语时使“并发”迭代成为可能。我的一位同事观察到，我们看到的问题很容易产生在代码中添加额外的、不需要的连接的解决方案，从而导致极其复杂的 API 边界很难正确地理清。这些都可以通过足够的努力来解决，但是当有人告诉你氛围编码本身就足够了时，你很难忽视这种体验，你只需将一个好的模型和工具指向一张票和一个代码库，然后让它撕裂。

sentences.en: Oh for vibe coding small scripts it's great.
sentences.zh: 哦，对于氛围编码小脚本来说，这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Experience of people with AI can vary, I don't see what attitude has to do with this, at this point I have probably spent thousands of hours trying different strategies to leverage LLMs in my workflows both for code and other artefacts, so one cannot say that I'm not enthusiastic or open towards this technology, I want it to work for me.
sentences.zh: 使用人工智能的人的经验可能会有所不同，我不明白这与什么态度有关，在这一点上，我可能花了数千个小时尝试不同的策略，在我的工作流程中利用法学硕士来处理代码和其他制品，所以不能说我对这项技术不热情或不开放，我希望它为我工作。

sentences.en: In some cases it works great and capabilities have increased a lot (the models I used two years ago seem so primitive by todays standards, I wonder how I could even have done work with them), but for me the tools still aren't good enough to be left writing products unsupervised.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，它工作得很好，而且功能也增加了很多（按照今天的标准，我两年前使用的模型似乎很原始，我想知道我怎么能用它们来完成工作），但对我来说，这些工具仍然不够好，无法在无人监督的情况下编写产品。

sentences.en: Maybe that is an attitude thing, but reading raw LLM generated text or code surfaces a lot of issues, and it requires heavy editing to make it meet the quality bar that I have.
sentences.zh: 也许这是一种态度问题，但阅读原始的 LLM 生成的文本或代码会出现很多问题，并且需要大量编辑才能使其达到我的质量标准。

sentences.en: I'm not the only one seeing it like that.
sentences.zh: 我不是唯一一个看到这种情况的人。

sentences.en: I could just throw that overboard and be happy, in the end I always make the LLM produce what I want, at least superficially, so like other people have suggested maybe I should just let go.I get that people without this mental baggage will adopt LLMs more easily as they do not care about any of these and they are often not able to perceive quality.
sentences.zh: 我可以把它扔到一边并感到高兴，最后我总是让法学硕士产生我想要的东西，至少是表面上的，所以就像其他人建议的那样，也许我应该放手。我知道没有这种精神包袱的人会更容易接受法学硕士，因为他们不关心这些，而且他们往往无法感知质量。

sentences.en: And maybe quality is something that doesn't even exist and doesn't matter much, in the end people don't care how the sausage is made and what is inside if it tastes good and nourishes them.
sentences.zh: 也许质量根本不存在，也无关紧要，最终人们并不关心香肠是如何制作的以及里面有什么，只要它味道好并且有营养。

sentences.en: It surprises me though how fast most "engineers" throw away their engineering principles when using these systems.
sentences.zh: 令我惊讶的是，大多数“工程师”在使用这些系统时抛弃他们的工程原理的速度有多快。

sentences.en: So I could also say mean things like maybe these people weren't good engineers to begin with.
sentences.zh: 所以我也可以说一些刻薄的话，比如也许这些人一开始就不是优秀的工程师。

sentences.en: I guess the divide is more between people that care about the underlying principles and quality of their work vs. people that care about being done and having the desired effect on the outside world through their work.
sentences.zh: 我想分歧更多的是关心工作基本原则和质量的人与关心工作完成并通过工作对外界产生预期影响的人。

sentences.en: For software that's more acceptable than in other engineering disciplines I guess, people won't get harmed (much) if your vibe coded SaaS app crashes or leaks your whole user database.
sentences.zh: 我想，对于比其他工程学科更容易接受的软件，如果您的 Vivi 编码 SaaS 应用程序崩溃或泄漏整个用户数据库，人们不会受到（太大）伤害。

sentences.en: Trust into vibe-coded software seems to be higher than I think is warranted though, which makes sense as the companies pour trillions of USD into marketing and getting people hooked on these systems.
sentences.zh: 不过，对振动编码软件的信任似乎比我想象的要高，这是有道理的，因为这些公司在营销上投入了数万亿美元，让人们对这些系统着迷。

sentences.en: Feels a bit like the whole crypto bubble, LLM absolutists aren't that different from crypto bros in 2015 that were certain traditional finance was doomed and in five years our entire life would play out on the blockchain.
sentences.zh: 感觉有点像整个加密货币泡沫，法学硕士绝对主义者与 2015 年的加密货币兄弟没有什么不同，当时传统金融注定要失败，五年后我们的整个生活将在区块链上展开。

sentences.en: I don't think it's entirely comparable though as LLMs have tons of real-world use cases.
sentences.zh: 我认为这并不完全具有可比性，因为法学硕士有大量的现实用例。

sentences.en: And I think it's not surprising that people have such strong opinions on them, there were similar discussions about Rust or frontend frameworks, seems in tech there are just types of people that discover something new and immediately think it will solve all of their issues and that anyone who has a different experience must be wrong, even though they are only seeing a tiny part of the whole problem space.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对它们有如此强烈的看法并不奇怪，关于 Rust 或前端框架也有类似的讨论，似乎在科技领域，只有一些人发现了一些新东西，并立即认为它会解决他们所有的问题，任何有不同经验的人都一定是错的，即使他们只看到了整个问题空间的一小部分。

sentences.en: So, glad people get value out of LLMs and I do too, but I don't get how one can use models and not see these quality issues.Maybe one point regarding quality, even for small scripts that I write using LLMs e.g. for data analysis I have to be very careful as they will often create subtle mistakes that ruin the whole analysis.
sentences.zh: 所以，很高兴人们从法学硕士中获得价值，我也是如此，但我不明白如何使用模型而不看到这些质量问题。也许有一点关于质量，即使对于我使用法学硕士编写的小脚本，例如对于数据分析，我必须非常小心，因为它们经常会产生微妙的错误，从而破坏整个分析。

sentences.en: Things that are not per se wrong as the script runs and produces the desired output (which the systems are optimized and trained for, i.e. they know how to create a script that works and kind of corresponds to the prompt), but in disciplines like data science where you need to think carefully about every step of an analysis LLMs are quite dangerous as they produce convincing looking results that seem correct at every stage but are completely wrong.
sentences.zh: 当脚本运行并产生所需的输出时，事情本身并没有错（系统为此进行了优化和训练，即它们知道如何创建一个可以工作并与提示相对应的脚本），但在数据科学等学科中，您需要仔细考虑分析的每一步，LLM 是相当危险的，因为它们产生的结果看起来令人信服，在每个阶段似乎都是正确的，但实际上是完全错误的。

sentences.en: The only way to get that right (in my experience) is to go really slowly testing each step individually with known good inputs and outputs, giving the LLM that as a harness to work in.I have been looking at LLM produced artefacts for a while now especially in data science and there are very cases where the models actually produced something entirely correct, at least when it's more complex than averaging some numbers or other simple things.
sentences.zh: 正确实现这一点的唯一方法（根据我的经验）是用已知的良好输入和输出单独缓慢地测试每个步骤，为 LLM 提供一个工作工具。我已经研究 LLM 产生的制品有一段时间了，尤其是在数据科学领域，在很多情况下，模型实际上产生了完全正确的东西，至少当它比平均一些数字或其他简单的东西更复杂时。

sentences.en: The same goes for writing, superficially it looks good but there are often subtle inconsistencies that the model just doesn't see and that are hard to spot.
sentences.zh: 写作也是如此，表面上看起来不错，但经常存在模型看不到且很难发现的微妙不一致之处。

sentences.en: And again, some people will just look at that and think "that's fine!"
sentences.zh: 再说一遍，有些人只会看着它并认为“没关系！”

sentences.en: because they just can't see the quality issues or they don't care about them, but that doesn't make these issues disappear...Think about it statistically, the benchmarks say clearly these models produce correct code in maybe 90-95 % of cases for most complex questions.
sentences.zh: 因为他们只是看不到质量问题，或者他们不关心这些问题，但这并不会让这些问题消失……从统计角度考虑，基准测试清楚地表明，对于最复杂的问题，这些模型可能在 90-95% 的情况下生成正确的代码。

sentences.en: That sounds high but given that a real-world system can consist of e.g. 100 such individual components then even a 99 % correctness rate at the level of an individual component gives you only a 36 % correctness rate for the entire system!
sentences.zh: 这听起来很高，但考虑到现实世界的系统可以由例如如果有 100 个这样的单独组件，那么即使单个组件的正确率达到 99%，整个系统的正确率也只有 36%！

sentences.en: That's also true for papers, presentations and anything else.
sentences.zh: 对于论文、演示文稿和其他任何东西来说也是如此。

sentences.en: Again, most people won't even understand this, for them something that looks correct and works is good enough.
sentences.zh: 同样，大多数人甚至不会理解这一点，对他们来说，看起来正确且有效的东西就足够了。

sentences.en: Yeah I have a lot of experience writing software.
sentences.zh: 是的，我有很多编写软件的经验。

sentences.en: My code is written mainly in Golang, but I had models write different code in Javascript, Rust, Python, Shell and other languages already.
sentences.zh: 我的代码主要是用 Golang 编写的，但我已经让模型用 Javascript、Rust、Python、Shell 和其他语言编写不同的代码。

sentences.en: I used a variety of frontier models over the last years, always the best available model at the time.I prompt LLMs by writing design specs and iterate on them first, then let it implement them step by step, checking the results after each step.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几年里，我使用了各种前沿模型，总是当时最好的可用模型。我通过编写设计规范来提示法学硕士，并首先对其进行迭代，然后让它一步步实现它们，每一步后检查结果。

sentences.en: That works fine for simpler changes where I use the LLM to write code that I have mostly worked out in my head, it always goes wrong once I try to do that with larger features.
sentences.zh: 这对于更简单的更改来说效果很好，我使用法学硕士来编写我大部分在脑海中解决的代码，但一旦我尝试使用更大的功能来做到这一点，它总是会出错。

sentences.en: I have tried a lot of different things like writing extensive RFCs and design docs for the whole codebase, building harnesses and evaluation loops to ensure we stick to specific paradigms in the codebases but the LLMs still deviate from that in sublte ways and spuriously introduce duplication, wrong abstractions or simple hacks.
sentences.zh: 我尝试了很多不同的事情，比如为整个代码库编写广泛的 RFC 和设计文档，构建工具和评估循环以确保我们坚持代码库中的特定范例，但法学硕士仍然以微妙的方式偏离了这一范式，并虚假地引入了重复、错误的抽象或简单的 hack。

sentences.en: That said my codebases are quite complex, it's not run of the mill CRUD software, I suspect these LLMs would do much better on these.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我的代码库相当复杂，它不是普通的 CRUD 软件，我怀疑这些法学硕士在这些方面会做得更好。

sentences.en: That's probably why other people report large success using AI based development, 90 % of apps out there are just plain RoR or Django backends, React or Next.js frontend or Android apps, and they are already built following strict cookie cutter recipes, LLMs have no trouble following these.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是为什么其他人报告使用基于 AI 的开发取得了巨大成功，90% 的应用程序只是简单的 RoR 或 Django 后端、React 或 Next.js 前端或 Android 应用程序，并且它们已经按照严格的千篇一律的食谱构建，法学硕士可以毫不费力地遵循这些。

sentences.en: My work is e.g. on novel parser generators, graph data persistence layers, format-preserving pseudonymization and personal information detection in unstructured data so there's really nothing that you can base the software design on apart from general principles, I suppose that is why the models struggle so much.There was a discussion here explaining the attention mechanism of the larger models and why they are not good at using their full context length, that was quite enlightening to me as it explained a lot of the behavior I saw on more complex changes, so I think one mistake I made was to have too long conversations with too much context (even though "on paper" the context length was fine and well within limits of the given model), I guess I need more careful conversation management and in general reduce the level of abstraction I'm working at with an LLM.
sentences.zh: 我的工作是例如关于新颖的解析器生成器、图形数据持久层、格式保留假名化和非结构化数据中的个人信息检测，因此除了一般原则之外，您实际上没有什么可以作为软件设计的基础，我想这就是模型如此挣扎的原因。这里有一个讨论解释了较大模型的注意力机制以及为什么它们不擅长使用其完整的上下文长度，这对我很有启发，因为它解释了我在更复杂的更改中看到的很多行为，所以我认为我犯的一个错误是与太多上下文进行太长的对话（即使“在纸上”，上下文长度很好并且完全在给定模型的限制之内），我想我需要更仔细的对话管理，并且通常会降低我与法学硕士一起工作的抽象水平。

sentences.en: For me at least they're not yet good enough to work at the business or concept level of abstraction, but they are capable of speeding up delivery of finished architectural designs.Maybe it's also a perception problem.
sentences.zh: 至少对我来说，它们还不够好，无法在业务或概念抽象级别上工作，但它们能够加快完成架构设计的交付速度。也许这也是一个感知问题。

sentences.en: A lot of people will just look at their AI generated software and check that it does what it's supposed to do on the happy path and they will be fine with that, calling it a day (and to be honest I did that too for projects with tight deadlines, though it feels irresponsible).
sentences.zh: 很多人只会查看他们的人工智能生成的软件，并检查它是否在快乐的道路上完成了应该做的事情，他们会对此感到满意，到此为止（说实话，对于期限紧迫的项目，我也这样做了，尽管这感觉不负责任）。

sentences.en: Especially juniors or people without programming background don't care about how the code looks that the AI wrote, I only see these issues because I have 10+ years of experience working by hand in large codebases and I have developed a "taste" for what good code is supposed to look like for me.
sentences.zh: 特别是初级人员或没有编程背景的人并不关心人工智能编写的代码看起来如何，我只看到这些问题，因为我有 10 多年在大型代码库中手工工作的经验，并且我已经形成了对我来说好的代码应该是什么样子的“品味”。

sentences.en: That might explain why people are feeling so radically different about LLMs, if you don't have all of that intrinsic baggage that senior level developers have amassed over their careers then AI generated code will always look good to you.
sentences.zh: 这也许可以解释为什么人们对法学硕士的感觉如此截然不同，如果你没有高级开发人员在职业生涯中积累的所有内在包袱，那么人工智能生成的代码对你来说总是很好。

sentences.en: And maybe they are right, could be that in 10 years no one looks at any code anymore and we just care about tests and making sure the behaviour is correct.
sentences.zh: 也许他们是对的，可能十年后没有人会再查看任何代码，我们只关心测试并确保行为正确。

sentences.en: To be honest I never looked at Assembly code in the last 10 years and I don't care how my compiler unrolls my loops (mostly) as it's a solved problem for me, maybe it will be similar with the higher level code, we just move the abstraction that we work at to a higher level.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我在过去 10 年里从未看过汇编代码，我也不关心我的编译器如何展开我的循环（大部分），因为这对我来说是一个已解决的问题，也许它与更高级别的代码类似，我们只是将我们工作的抽象移到更高的级别。

sentences.en: But I still feel that we don't have the right tools for working at this higher level yet.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然觉得我们还没有合适的工具来在这个更高的层面上工作。

sentences.en: The test is simple: have we seen great new products or improvements in the products we use over the past 12,24,36 months?The only great new product I’ve used is my LLM of choice, and those labs seem to be hiring more humans than ever.Maybe it’s true that Claude only just got good enough and that 12 months from now our day to day lives will be way better thanks to LLM-driven product improvements/breakthroughs.My bet is that 12 months from now we will still have no great improvements and the claim will be “LLMs only got good enough in Feb 2027 so you can’t judge anything yet!”
sentences.zh: 测试很简单：在过去的 12、24、36 个月中，我们是否看到了很棒的新产品或我们使用的产品的改进？我使用过的唯一很棒的新产品是我选择的法学硕士，而这些实验室似乎比以往雇用了更多的人员。也许克劳德只是刚刚足够好，从现在起 12 个月后，由于法学硕士驱动的产品改进/突破，我们的日常生活将会变得更好。我打赌，从现在起 12 个月后我们仍然不会有很大的改进，并且声明将是“法学硕士在 2027 年 2 月才足够好，所以你还不能判断任何事情！”

sentences.en: I have a similar one.
sentences.zh: 我有一个类似的。

sentences.en: Is Claude Code (web and/or VS Code) still a buggy mess?
sentences.zh: Claude Code（Web 和/或 VS Code）仍然是一个充满 bug 的混乱吗？

sentences.en: Pretty much every single agent loop bugs out and requires a hard refresh, which sometimes still doesn’t help.
sentences.zh: 几乎每个代理循环都会出现错误并需要硬刷新，但这有时仍然没有帮助。

sentences.en: And they have an effectively infinite LLM budget and unreleased models to fix the issues.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有有效无限的法学硕士预算和未发布的模型来解决这些问题。

sentences.en: Even Pi sucks.
sentences.zh: 就连Pi也很烂。

sentences.en: I can no longer get it to open.
sentences.zh: 我再也无法打开它了。

sentences.en: OpenCode sometimes consumes all my 32Gb of memory.
sentences.zh: OpenCode 有时会耗尽我所有的 32Gb 内存。

sentences.en: Codex sometimes doesn't display the full output (display issue).
sentences.zh: Codex 有时不显示完整的输出（显示问题）。

sentences.en: I stopped using Claude Code because of how unpredictable their agent is (and it is very opaque about what it is doing).
sentences.zh: 我停止使用 Claude Code 因为他们的代理是多么不可预测（而且它在做什么非常不透明）。

sentences.en: I don't even get to how many times I run a prompt and then the response is stopped mid-way.
sentences.zh: 我什至不知道我运行了多少次提示，然后响应中途停止了。

sentences.en: The whole industry is a joke.
sentences.zh: 整个行业就是个笑话。

sentences.en: Disclaimer: I am not an LLM maximalist, I like to use LLMs, but in a highly controlled way.One exciting development that LLMs have recently started is automated vulnerability discovery.
sentences.zh: 免责声明：我不是法学硕士的最高主义者，我喜欢使用法学硕士，但以高度控制的方式使用法学硕士。法学硕士最近开始的一项令人兴奋的发展是自动漏洞发现。

sentences.en: For instance, Chrome solved more bugs in June than over the past two years:https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49120097Similarly, the latest Apple security update and the June Android Security Bulletin fixes an insane number of vulnerabilities.Of course, many of these vulnerabilities are caused by using unsafe languages (C/C++).
sentences.zh: 例如，Chrome 在 6 月份解决的 bug 数量比过去两年还要多：https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49120097 同样，最新的 Apple 安全更新和 6 月份 Android 安全公告修复了数量惊人的漏洞。当然，其中许多漏洞是由于使用不安全语言（C/C++）造成的。

sentences.en: But LLMs also help porting such code to Rust or other safe languages, because it is the type of transformation that LLMs are pretty good at (clearly defined problem, not many opportunities to go wild).
sentences.zh: 但法学硕士还有助于将此类代码移植到 Rust 或其他安全语言，因为这是法学硕士非常擅长的转换类型（明确定义的问题，没有太多机会去疯狂）。

sentences.en: Yeah I can see this as being an area that will benefit from LLMs.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个将从法学硕士中受益的领域。

sentences.en: Though, taking it one further, we don’t yet have evidence (so far as I know) that this actually produces more secure software.It’s not that I’m an LLM hater at all, I use them, I feel like I’m being super productive so I’m not doubting people’s accounts.
sentences.zh: 不过，更进一步来说，我们还没有证据（据我所知）这实际上可以生产出更安全的软件。这并不是说我讨厌 LLM，我使用它们，我觉得我的生产力非常高，所以我不会怀疑人们的账户。

sentences.en: But if I honestly look back over the past 12 months and ask “have I shipped more value that I would have without LLMs” the answer is probably no.I think it has helped me learn areas quicker, though for complex mathsy explanations I still ask for it to find me human written posts as Claude’s explanations can be super weird, using convoluted analogies etc..
sentences.zh: 但如果我诚实地回顾过去 12 个月并问“我是否比没有 LLM 获得了更多价值”，答案可能是否定的。我认为它帮助我更快地学习领域，尽管对于复杂的数学解释，我仍然要求它为我找到人工撰写的帖子，因为克劳德的解释可能非常奇怪，使用令人费解的类比等。

sentences.en: I am launching projects at about the same rate, but the projects are much more polished and feature full than before AI tools.Historically, the mindset was to get happy path working launch and see what works, but now you can ship a much more polished products with things like cancellation and account export, private policies, a entire mobile and web app without much effort. > The test is simple: have we seen great new products or improvements in the products we use over the past 12,24,36 months?I'd say it only became viable end of last year but yes, recently there's a surge of hobbist software which is very visible.How well they will be maintained, that's another story Can you name a few?
sentences.zh: 我正在以大致相同的速度启动项目，但这些项目比以前的人工智能工具更加精致和功能齐全。从历史上看，人们的心态是获得快乐的启动方式，看看什么有效，但现在你可以毫不费力地发布更精致的产品，包括取消和帐户导出、私人政策、整个移动和网络应用程序。 > 测试很简单：我们是否看到了过去 12、24、36 个月中我们使用的产品的出色新产品或改进？我想说它直到去年年底才变得可行，但是是的，最近出现了非常明显的 Hobbist 软件激增。它们的维护情况如何，那是另一个故事了，您能举几个例子吗？

sentences.en: Not doubting your claim, just curious because I am maybe not following the same niches you do.
sentences.zh: 不是怀疑你的说法，只是好奇，因为我可能不遵循你所关注的同样的利基市场。

sentences.en: I can think few great tools like t3code (a software that does a lot) that have been mostly coded by LLMs and yet have a solid architectural foundation and implementation.
sentences.zh: 我认为很少有像 t3code（一款功能丰富的软件）这样的优秀工具，它们主要由法学硕士编写，但具有坚实的架构基础和实现。

sentences.en: The software is genuinely gargantuan in its features and capability, you really cannot appreciate it from quickly skimming the readme.At work, LLMs helped a lot in doing the kind of work you were always tired or had no budget to do, and the codebases have never been healthier, more tested and better documented.In any case, it's always about the effort and capabilities of the people using it.
sentences.zh: 该软件的特性和功能确实非常庞大，你真的无法通过快速浏览自述文件​​来欣赏它。在工作中，法学硕士在完成那些你总是感到疲倦或没有预算的工作方面提供了很多帮助，而且代码库从未如此健康、经过更多测试和更好地记录。无论如何，它总是与使用它的人的努力和能力有关。

sentences.en: If you want to vibecode, then you're still stuck in prototype land and I think that even better models won't help, in fact they may have negative value.The naivety of your post is in any case appalling, you seem to be missing the forest for the tree.
sentences.zh: 如果你想进行 vivicode，那么你仍然停留在原型领域，我认为即使更好的模型也无济于事，事实上它们可能具有负面价值。你的帖子的天真无论如何都是令人震惊的，你似乎只见树木不见森林。

sentences.en: What’s naive about it?
sentences.zh: 这有什么天真呢？

sentences.en: Maybe a bunch of people are finding great new software only possible because of LLMs.
sentences.zh: 也许很多人会因为法学硕士而发现伟大的新软件。

sentences.en: Good for them.
sentences.zh: 对他们有好处。

sentences.en: I’m simply stating I haven’t.(I note in your comment you don’t mention one piece of end user software or how the user has benefitted…) > have we seen great new products or improvements in the products we use over the past 12,24,36 monthsThis sentiment drives me nuts.I'm on a handful of software dev subreddits and the amount of new products popping up has tripled since these tools became available.I also don't understand how you'd expect to measure this.
sentences.zh: 我只是简单地说我没有。（我注意到在你的评论中你没有提到一款最终用户软件或用户如何受益......）>我们在过去的12、24、36个月中是否看到了伟大的新产品或我们使用的产品的改进这种情绪让我发疯。我在一些软件开发子版块上，自从这些工具可用以来，弹出的新产品数量增加了两倍。我也不明白你希望如何衡量这一点。

sentences.en: Is there some single list of all software that's been released that annotates whether AI was used?
sentences.zh: 是否有已发布的所有软件的单一列表来注释是否使用了人工智能？

sentences.en: Do you have some feed of every project that hits GitHub that you're meticulously tracking?
sentences.zh: 您是否有您正在仔细跟踪的每个访问 GitHub 的项目的摘要？

sentences.en: The idea that you personally should have seen these improvements or they didn't happen is wild to me.I work in healthcare.
sentences.zh: “你个人应该看到这些改进，或者它们没有发生”的想法对我来说很疯狂。我在医疗保健行业工作。

sentences.en: Where the # of products has skyrocketed due to these tools.
sentences.zh: 由于这些工具，产品数量猛增。

sentences.en: Some are bad, some are good.
sentences.zh: 有些是坏的，有些是好的。

sentences.en: But to say that nothing has come out of it is just objectively not true.
sentences.zh: 但说没有任何结果，客观上是不正确的。

sentences.en: There's a staggering amount of new, basic software which often goes unmaintained quickly because no discipline was needed to build it.
sentences.zh: 有数量惊人的新的基础软件往往很快就会失去维护，因为构建它们不需要任何纪律。

sentences.en: But I don't think we're seeing, for example, Adobe releasing new creative suite tools faster than before.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们并没有看到 Adob​​e 比以前更快地发布新的创意套件工具。

sentences.en: This isn't something I can quite quantify, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这不是我可以完全量化的事情。

sentences.en: What industry are you in and what's your role?
sentences.zh: 您从事什么行业？您的角色是什么？

sentences.en: There are new EMR's popping up overnight in healthcare.
sentences.zh: 医疗保健领域一夜之间出现了新的电子病历。

sentences.en: And that's my point.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的观点。

sentences.en: There's no way a person can say that it's not happening because they personally aren't seeing it.
sentences.zh: 一个人不可能因为他们个人没有看到它而说它没有发生。

sentences.en: Thinking in terms of "Well why aren't the big companies building software quicker" answers it's own questions.
sentences.zh: 从“为什么大公司不更快地构建软件”的角度思考可以回答它自己的问题。

sentences.en: It wasn't the coding that was making it slow. > There are new EMR's popping up overnight in healthcareThat's probably the last place I want AI generated bullshit to be popping up overnight > I'm on a handful of software dev subreddits and the amount of new products popping up has tripled since these tools became available.> I also don't understand how you'd expect to measure thisI'm confused, are we accepting anecdata or no?
