sentences.zh: 导致速度变慢的并不是编码。 > 医疗保健领域一夜之间出现了新的电子病历，这可能是我最不希望人工智能生成的废话一夜之间出现的地方 > 我在一些软件开发子版块上，自从这些工具可用以来，新产品的数量增加了两倍。 > 我也不明白你希望如何衡量这一点。我很困惑，我们是否接受轶事数据？

sentences.en: Products, yes, because the barrier to making a product had fallen off a cliff (both in developing the software and the marketing/sales fluff around it).
sentences.zh: 产品，是的，因为制造产品的障碍已经跌落悬崖（无论是开发软件还是围绕它的营销/销售）。

sentences.en: But are those products converting to business results?
sentences.zh: 但这些产品能否转化为业务成果？

sentences.en: Are those quality products someone will pay for?In other words, is anyone using these products or is that becoming like the spammy App Stores with tons of low effort stuff? > But are those products converting to business results?
sentences.zh: 这些优质产品是否有人愿意付费？换句话说，是否有人使用这些产品，或者这些产品是否会变得像垃圾邮件应用商店一样，提供大量低效的东西？ > 但这些产品是否能转化为业务成果？

sentences.en: Are those quality products someone will pay for?Yes.
sentences.zh: 这些优质产品有人愿意花钱买吗？是的。

sentences.en: Unequivocally.I'm in healthcare.
sentences.zh: 明确地说，我从事医疗保健行业。

sentences.en: I've sat in 20-30 different demos over the last 2 years, all of which involve AI in some capacity and at least half of those were solutions that had already built a customer base.But a lot of devs won't know that because they aren't sitting in meetings where product decisions are made.
sentences.zh: 在过去的两年里，我参加了 20-30 个不同的演示，所有这些演示都在一定程度上涉及人工智能，其中至少有一半是已经建立了客户群的解决方案。但很多开发人员不会知道这一点，因为他们没有参加制定产品决策的会议。

sentences.en: I'm in a unique position, but that doesn't meet it's not happening.
sentences.zh: 我处于一个独特的位置，但这并不符合它不会发生的情况。

sentences.en: It's the opposite: people like you will be telling people using these tools successfully, "but where are all great new products???", which, of course, is almost immeasurable.The Internet is a better fax machine and all that.
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反：像您这样的人会告诉人们成功地使用这些工具，“但是伟大的新产品在哪里？？？”，这当然几乎是不可估量的。互联网是更好的传真机等等。

sentences.en: Who is using them successfully and what _are_ the great new products?Examples, please.
sentences.zh: 谁在成功使用它们？什么是伟大的新产品？请举例。

sentences.en: It's easy to prove your point if it's true.
sentences.zh: 如果你的观点是正确的，那么很容易证明你的观点。

sentences.en: This question is a trap.
sentences.zh: 这个问题是一个陷阱。

sentences.en: Like programming languages.
sentences.zh: 就像编程语言一样。

sentences.en: There's the products everybody hates and the ones nobody uses.
sentences.zh: 有些产品人人都讨厌，有些产品没人使用。

sentences.en: When you have built your working product try this prompt:- Review the codebase is it production ready?
sentences.zh: 当您构建了工作产品后，请尝试此提示：- 检查代码库是否已准备好投入生产？

sentences.en: I'm selling it for $1million dollars can it meet that standard.Then cry as the ai reveals that it didn't actually do anything close to what it said it did.
sentences.zh: 我以 100 万美元的价格出售它，它能满足这个标准吗？然后当人工智能透露它实际上并没有做任何与它所说的相近的事情时，我哭了。

sentences.en: I call this my million dollar prompt, as in it teaches you just how much you are being fooled.
sentences.zh: 我把这称为我的百万美元提示，因为它告诉你你被愚弄了多少。

sentences.en: Popped over to HackerNews, read two comment sections and the top comments in both articles were users saying the same thing: "AI can't write code!
sentences.zh: 跳到 HackerNews，阅读两个评论部分，两篇文章中最热门的评论都是用户说同样的话：“AI 不会写代码！

sentences.en: The whole thing will come crumbling down any minute!
sentences.zh: 整个事情随时都会崩溃！

sentences.en: Just you wait!"I've never seen this community like this.
sentences.zh: 你等着吧！”我从来没有见过这样的社区。

sentences.en: Are these people cooked?
sentences.zh: 这些人都煮熟了？

sentences.en: We are years into this and they haven't been able to figure it out?
sentences.zh: 我们已经研究了很多年了，他们还没有弄清楚吗？

sentences.en: They are going to continue to tell people using these tools successfully every day that, actually, it's just a mirage?
sentences.zh: 他们将继续告诉每天成功使用这些工具的人们，实际上，这只是海市蜃楼？

sentences.en: I highly suspect they are real humans being paid to do it.
sentences.zh: 我高度怀疑他们是受雇做这件事的真人。

sentences.en: AI will have produced a much more detectable result.
sentences.zh: 人工智能将产生更容易检测的结果。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's baffling.
sentences.zh: 是的，这令人困惑。

sentences.en: I can't relate to these statements at all.
sentences.zh: 我根本无法理解这些说法。

sentences.en: What are people doing?
sentences.zh: 人们在做什么？

sentences.en: Surely the smart people of HN would have been able to figure this out a long time ago.I also don't find these people in real life.
sentences.zh: 当然，HN 的聪明人早就能想到这一点了。我在现实生活中也找不到这些人。

sentences.en: Even the most junior developers I know are able to navigate this without creating this supposed mess.
sentences.zh: 即使是我认识的最初级的开发人员也能够解决这个问题，而不会造成这种所谓的混乱。

sentences.en: Its a bit unkind to talk like this - the obvious and equally unproductive response is to question if you are really as good as you think you are.
sentences.zh: 这样说话有点不友善——显而易见且同样没有成效的回应是质疑你是否真的像你想象的那么好。

sentences.en: Are those junior developers not making a mess, or do you lack the insight to see it?
sentences.zh: 是那些初级开发人员没有搞乱，还是你缺乏洞察力？

sentences.en: Big codebases tend to become a mess anyway so if your company has experience dealing with shit, the fact that now shit is AI-generated doesn't substantially change anything.And I'm not joking.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，大的代码库往往会变得一团糟，所以如果你的公司有处理垃圾的经验，那么现在垃圾是人工智能生成的事实并不会实质性改变任何东西。我不是在开玩笑。

sentences.en: Imagine it this way - managing a group of skilled professionals is a completely different skill from managing a bunch of alcoholics doing a minimum-wage job, and sometimes the latter situation is just the reality you find yourself in.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，管理一群熟练的专业人士与管理一群从事最低工资工作的酗酒者是完全不同的技能，有时后一种情况正是你发现自己所处的现实。

sentences.en: But if so, then where is the secret prompt sauce for getting those results, please?
sentences.zh: 但如果是这样，那么获得这些结果的秘密提示在哪里？

sentences.en: It's not like we complainers don't read and put in practice all we can about how to refine a spec prompt after prompt, yet our results are still disappointing.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说我们抱怨者没有阅读并实践我们所能学到的一切关于如何在提示后完善规范提示的信息，但我们的结果仍然令人失望。

sentences.en: To me, that's no wonder at all, as we haven't reached AGI yet; hence, no matter how impressive and productive these tools are, I totally don't expect them to actually know what they are doing.To be clear: LLMs write about 99% of my code, but with constant steering.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这根本不奇怪，因为我们还没有达到 AGI；因此，无论这些工具多么令人印象深刻和高效，我完全不希望它们真正知道自己在做什么。需要明确的是：LLM 编写了我大约 99% 的代码，但需要不断的指导。

sentences.en: A lot of this is just talking past each other.
sentences.zh: 很多事情只是互相说说而已。

sentences.en: AI being good enough to write 99% of your code but then you still complain about it sucking.
sentences.zh: AI 足以编写你 99% 的代码，但你仍然抱怨它很糟糕。

sentences.en: Glass half full vs half empty.
sentences.zh: 玻璃杯半满与半空。

sentences.en: I've seen two camps of people within the same company I work at.
sentences.zh: 我在我工作的同一家公司见过两个阵营的人。

sentences.en: Some think AI is generating acceptable code.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为人工智能正在生成可接受的代码。

sentences.en: Others think it's generating slop.I sit in the middle a lot of the time as my opinion on code quality vary depending on how important the code actually is.I will say one thing, the people who I generally deemed as worse developers prior to the wide AI roll out are the ones that are more accepting of AI code.
sentences.zh: 其他人认为这会产生混乱。我很多时候都处于中间位置，因为我对代码质量的看法取决于代码实际的重要性。我会说一件事，在广泛的人工智能推出之前，我通常认为开发人员较差的人是那些更容易接受人工智能代码的人。

sentences.en: And consequently, they're the ones spending a magnitude more money each day.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们每天花的钱要多得多。

sentences.en: The people who were writing better code and, in my opinion, were stronger developers, are spending less on AI and are generating more acceptable code when they use it.
sentences.zh: 那些编写更好代码的人，在我看来，是更强大的开发人员，在人工智能上花费更少，并且在使用人工智能时生成更可接受的代码。

sentences.en: And they can spot issues from a mile away, because they actually understand the code being generated.
sentences.zh: 他们可以在一英里之外发现问题，因为他们实际上理解正在生成的代码。

sentences.en: They're not just committing lots of redundant code.We had an AI outage for a day or two a few weeks back.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅仅是提交大量冗余代码。几周前，我们的人工智能出现了一两天的故障。

sentences.en: The reaction from some people was like it was the end of the world and they couldn't do any work.
sentences.zh: 有些人的反应就像世界末日一样，他们无法做任何工作。

sentences.en: Some projects got put on hold because no one actually knew how to work on the code base without AI.
sentences.zh: 一些项目被搁置，因为没有人真正知道如何在没有人工智能的情况下在代码库上工作。

sentences.en: Other, better in my opinion, developers just went shrugged it off and got on with their job.AI over-dependence is a big issue that people will face more and more.
sentences.zh: 其他的，在我看来更好的是，开发人员只是耸耸肩，继续他们的工作。人工智能的过度依赖是人们将越来越多地面临的一个大问题。

sentences.en: Weaker juniors used to just be a bit slower and stagnate a bit, but they could still kinda work independently and understand what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 较弱的初级人员过去只是速度有点慢，有点停滞，但他们仍然可以独立工作并理解自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Now they are almost entirely prompt monkeys, take away their Claude Code terminal and they are completely stumped. > I sit in the middle a lot of the time as my opinion on code quality vary depending on how important the code actually is.This is really the key insight that most people on the extreme ends of the discussion don't seem to grasp and then talk in absolutisms because they think that their tiny village is the whole world.It's the same kind of 'extremism' that dominates most discussions about memory safety btw.For some types of programs, code quality simply doesn't matter as long the program does its job, and generating those programs even with the most sloppiest vibecoding approaches is totally fine.And in some areas of the industry (like web development) these types of programs are basically the norm - but this sort of code was already mostly hastily cobbled together slop even before AI.I also see extreme differences in usefulness of LLM code generation.
sentences.zh: 现在他们几乎完全是敏捷的猴子，拿走他们的克劳德代码终端，他们就完全被难住了。 > 我很多时候都坐在中间，因为我对代码质量的看法取决于代码实际的重要性。这确实是大多数处于讨论极端的人似乎没有掌握的关键见解，然后用绝对论来谈论，因为他们认为他们的小村庄就是整个世界。顺便说一句，这与主导大多数有关内存安全的讨论的“极端主义”是一样的。对于某些类型的程序，只要程序完成其工作，代码质量根本不重要，并且即使使用最草率的vibecoding方法生成这些程序也是完全没问题的。在行业的某些领域（如Web开发），这些类型的程序基本上是常态——但这种代码甚至在人工智能出现之前就已经大部分被匆忙拼凑在一起。我还看到LLM代码生成的实用性存在极大差异。

sentences.en: For anything JS or TS it works great because there's a giant corpus.
sentences.zh: 对于任何 JS 或 TS 来说，它都非常有效，因为有一个巨大的语料库。

sentences.en: For C code (or even more obscure languages) especially when using libraries which change all the time my experience is totally different (at least for code generation, bug scanning works quite well).That's my experience so far anyway, literally "hit and miss" with some areas where there are more hits than misses, and other areas where it's the other way around.
sentences.zh: 对于 C 代码（甚至更晦涩的语言），特别是当使用一直在变化的库时，我的体验完全不同（至少对于代码生成来说，错误扫描效果很好）。无论如何，这就是我到目前为止的经验，字面意思是“命中和未命中”，某些区域命中多于未命中，而其他区域则相反。

sentences.en: It’s not a mess as in spaghetti code, which you will find with novice programmers.
sentences.zh: 它不像新手程序员会发现的意大利面条代码那样混乱。

sentences.en: It’s a mess as in complex and disjointed codebase.
sentences.zh: 就像复杂且脱节的代码库一样，一团糟。

sentences.en: Happy path works somewhat, but it crumbles if you run it long enough or encounters an edge case.You need a very good level of insight to build a codebase to do what is supposed to do, to not do what it shouldn’t do, and to still be comprehensible.
sentences.zh: 快乐路径在某种程度上有效，但如果你运行它足够长的时间或遇到边缘情况，它就会崩溃。你需要非常好的洞察力来构建代码库来做应该做的事情，不做不应该做的事情，并且仍然可以理解。

sentences.en: Because a software is a system and building system well is what engineering is about.
sentences.zh: 因为软件是一个系统，而构建好系统就是工程的意义所在。

sentences.en: Isn't "spaghetti code" a casual term to describe "complex and disjointed codebase"?
sentences.zh: “意大利面条代码”不是一个用来描述“复杂且脱节的代码库”的随意术语吗？

sentences.en: What's the difference?
sentences.zh: 有什么区别？

sentences.en: Have I been using the term wrong all this time?
sentences.zh: 我一直以来都用错了这个词吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 并不真地。

sentences.en: Spaghetti code is usually related to the big ball of mud.
sentences.zh: 意大利面条式代码通常与大泥球有关。

sentences.en: Meaning anything you need to understand, you need to go up and down the files while being distracted by irrelevant concerns.
sentences.zh: 意味着您需要理解的任何内容，您都需要上下查看文件，同时被不相关的问题分散注意力。

sentences.en: There’s no abstraction, no separation of concerns,…Complex and disjointed codebase is the usual over engineering.
sentences.zh: 没有抽象，没有关注点分离……复杂且脱节的代码库是工程中常见的情况。

sentences.en: The requirement calls for a quick printf, but the implemented module is equivalent to ncurses.
sentences.zh: 该需求需要一个快速的 printf，但实现的模块相当于 ncurses。

sentences.en: And then every calling point turns into a complex ceremony.
sentences.zh: 然后每个呼叫点都变成了一个复杂的仪式。

sentences.en: And most of them are subtly wrong in some way.Those are two distinct mode of failures.
sentences.zh: 他们中的大多数在某种程度上都存在微妙的错误。这是两种不同的失败模式。

sentences.en: The first was the sin of novice programmers before LLM.
sentences.zh: 第一个是LLM之前新手程序员的罪孽。

sentences.en: The second was the sin of not so novice programmers before LLMs, at least until the pain of living with their mistakes taught them better.But with agentic tooling, the output is often the second.
sentences.zh: 第二个是法学硕士之前的新手程序员所犯的罪，至少在忍受错误的痛苦教会他们更好之前是这样。但使用代理工具，输出通常是第二个。

sentences.en: I believe mostly because no one publish the simple generic version of their codebase.
sentences.zh: 我相信主要是因为没有人发布其代码库的简单通用版本。

sentences.en: Instead it’s the one that is aligned with their specs, simple in that context, but too complex in any other.
sentences.zh: 相反，它是符合他们的规格的，在这种情况下很简单，但在其他任何情况下都太复杂。

sentences.en: Says more about you buddy.
sentences.zh: 说了更多关于你的事情，伙计。

sentences.en: I didn't say I'm anti AI.
sentences.zh: 我没说我反对人工智能。

sentences.en: I said run the prompt.
sentences.zh: 我说运行提示。

sentences.en: If you had run the prompt then you would now have better code.
sentences.zh: 如果您运行了提示符，那么您现在将拥有更好的代码。

sentences.en: Instead you decided to spark off some dumb debate that has nothing to do with what I said in my comment.Kind of ironic no?
sentences.zh: 相反，你决定引发一些愚蠢的辩论，与我在评论中所说的无关。有点讽刺不是吗？

sentences.en: To be the harbinger of the very thing you object to.
sentences.zh: 成为你所反对的事情的先兆。

sentences.en: I've posted this before and it's still what I think:I'm convinced that the polarization is that one's impression of AI has a direct 1:1 mapping with one's previous level of skill and sensitivity to quality.
sentences.zh: 我之前已经发过这篇文章，现在仍然是我的想法：我确信两极分化是一个人对人工智能的印象与一个人以前的技能水平和对质量的敏感度有直接的 1:1 映射。

sentences.en: Most people are by definition average and they are impressed.Is there anyone in the industry noted for their skill, quality, and taste, e.g. Jonathon Blow, Casey Muratori, who is impressed and thinks the AI is really good?
sentences.zh: 大多数人都是平均水平，他们对此印象深刻。业内是否有任何人因其技能、品质和品味而闻名，例如Jonathon Blow、Casey Muratori，谁印象深刻并认为人工智能真的很好？

sentences.en: I haven't seen any.
sentences.zh: 我还没见过。

sentences.en: In my personal circle, the best devs I know are either micromanaging or shunning AI; none of them think the agents are capable or really good.
sentences.zh: 在我的个人圈子里，我认识的最好的开发人员要么进行微观管理，要么回避人工智能；他们都不认为这些特工有能力或者真的很优秀。

sentences.en: The mediocre devs I know are largely on board.
sentences.zh: 我认识的平庸的开发人员大部分都参与其中。

sentences.en: This applies both online and off.Couple this with the fact that no AI focused project has come out, not a single one, that meets a high quality bar with nontrivial complexity.I am an AI quality sceptic.
sentences.zh: 这在线上和线下都适用。事实上，还没有一个以人工智能为重点的项目问世，没有一个项目能够满足高质量标准和不平凡的复杂性。我是人工智能质量怀疑论者。

sentences.en: They can be useful if you don't care for quality, but I never don't care for quality.
sentences.zh: 如果你不关心质量，它们可能很有用，但我从来不关心质量。

sentences.en: I live for quality. > The whole thing will come crumbling down any minuteIt is crumbling down as we speak.
sentences.zh: 我为品质而生。 > 整个事情随时都会崩溃，就在我们说话的时候，它正在崩溃。

sentences.en: There's more software being pumped out than ever, but it's also buggier, more bloated, and just generally worse than ever.A few days ago I had to revert to an older version of an open source project I use regularly, because the author turned full vibe coder and has pushed hundreds of AI generated commits in just a few weeks, at least one of which completely broke an important feature I relied on.Whether or not you consider putting out software that technically meets the minimum requirements but is a buggy, broken mess to be a success depends entirely on your personal definition of success.
sentences.zh: 推出的软件比以往任何时候都多，但问题也更多、更臃肿，而且总体上比以往更糟糕。几天前，我不得不恢复到我经常使用的一个开源项目的旧版本，因为作者变成了完整的vibe编码器，并在短短几周内推送了数百个人工智能生成的提交，其中至少有一个完全破坏了我所依赖的一个重要功能。您是否考虑推出技术上满足最低要求的软件，但它是一个有缺陷、破碎的烂摊子是否成功完全取决于你个人对成功的定义。

sentences.en: Maybe you do, and you are entitled to your opinion.
sentences.zh: 也许你会这样做，并且你有权发表你的意见。

sentences.en: But once again I feel the need to remind people that we humans did not get where we are today by always doing the bare minimum.
sentences.zh: 但我再次觉得有必要提醒人们，我们人类并不是通过总是做最低限度的事情而取得今天的成就。

sentences.en: If everyone throughout history shared this mentality, we'd still be banging rocks in caves. > also buggier, more bloated, and just generally worse than ever.Citation needed.
sentences.zh: 如果历史上每个人都持有这种心态，我们仍然会在山洞里敲石头。 > 也更加错误，更加臃肿，而且总体上比以往更糟糕。需要引用。

sentences.en: I have seen enormous improvements in bug fixes across our projects and many other companies (one HN headline says Google fixed more bugs in July than in previous 2 years).
sentences.zh: 我看到我们的项目和许多其他公司在错误修复方面取得了巨大的进步（HN 的一则标题称谷歌在 7 月份修复的错误比前两年还要多）。

sentences.en: I would’ve expected even more given how easy it is to fix things now.
sentences.zh: 考虑到现在解决问题是多么容易，我本来期望更多。

sentences.en: LLMs can understand code better than anyone I’ve met, judging by their power to explain something and then optionally go ahead and fix stuff.
sentences.zh: 法学硕士比我见过的任何人都能更好地理解代码，从他们解释某些事情然后选择性地继续修复问题的能力来看。

sentences.en: People used to ask me about our project as I am the most senior developer and been working on our product for 12 years.
sentences.zh: 人们过去常常向我询问我们的项目，因为我是最资深的开发人员，并且在我们的产品上工作了 12 年。

sentences.en: But when I want to know something for sure I myself ask Claude.
sentences.zh: 但当我想确切地知道一些事情时，我自己就会问克劳德。

sentences.en: It is amazingly good. > Citation needed.that's not where the burden of proof lies buddy.
sentences.zh: 这是令人惊讶的好。 > 需要引用。这不是举证责任的地方，伙计。

sentences.en: you prove to us where AI has caused a spike in quality, functioning software > Citation needed.Citation is me and my own personal experiences with vibe coded software.
sentences.zh: 你向我们证明了人工智能在何处导致了质量、功能软件的飞跃 > 需要引用。引用是我和我自己使用氛围编码软件的个人经历。

sentences.en: If you have examples of stable, efficient, polished software created by AI, I'll gladly try them out.Regardless, your comment is a perfect exhibit of the problem.
sentences.zh: 如果您有人工智能创建的稳定、高效、精美的软件示例，我很乐意尝试一下。无论如何，您的评论完美地展示了问题。

sentences.en: You are seeing 100 AI generated PRs merged in a day and interpreting that as 100 improvements to the user experience, which probably sounds great when you tell it to your manager before asking for a promotion, but doesn't actually translate to reality and never has.
sentences.zh: 你会看到一天内合并了 100 个 AI 生成的 PR，并将其解释为对用户体验的 100 项改进，当你在要求升职之前告诉你的经理时，这可能听起来很棒，但实际上并没有转化为现实，而且从未转化为现实。

sentences.en: Before AI, it was generally agreed upon that measuring quality of work by lines of code written, PRs merged, etc. made no sense, yet that wisdom seems to have been completely forgotten in favor of just watching the line go up.How do you even know the improvements are "enormous" if you don't understand the code?
sentences.zh: 在人工智能出现之前，人们普遍认为通过编写的代码行数、合并的 PR 等来衡量工作质量是没有意义的，但这种智慧似乎已经完全被遗忘，而只看代码的上升。如果你不理解代码，你怎么知道改进是“巨大的”？

sentences.en: Do you just occasionally glance at your terminal to see Claude going on about how it just found the smoking gun and made a critical fix to a load-bearing seam and go "whoa, that sounds important"?
sentences.zh: 您是否只是偶尔瞥一眼您的终端，看到 Claude 正在讲述它如何找到确凿证据并对承重接缝进行关键修复，然后说“哇，这听起来很重要”？

sentences.en: If those improvements and bug fixes really were so important, why were they not considered worth the effort to make before AI came along, or was your team simply incapable of making them before?If you're the most senior developer working on the same codebase for 12 years, yet proudly state that an LLM understands it better than you do, I can't help but interpret that as an admission of incompetence, so letting AI do your work for you may really be an improvement, but it shouldn't be.
sentences.zh: 如果这些改进和错误修复真的如此重要，为什么在人工智能出现之前不值得付出努力，或者你的团队以前根本没有能力做到这些？如果你是在同一代码库上工作了 12 年的最资深开发人员，却自豪地宣称法学硕士比你更了解它，我不禁将其解释为承认你的无能，所以让人工智能为你做你的工作可能确实是一种进步，但不应该如此。

sentences.en: Adminer.
sentences.zh: 行政。

sentences.en: The code was never great, but it worked, and I have not been able to find a suitable replacement that isn't slow and bloated.The specific functionality that was broken was the plugin that allows picking from a fixed list of servers instead of entering the address every time.
sentences.zh: 代码从来都不是很好，但它有效，而且我一直无法找到一个既不慢又不臃肿的合适替代品。被破坏的具体功能是允许从固定服务器列表中进行选择而不是每次都输入地址的插件。

sentences.en: Zero.
sentences.zh: 零。

sentences.en: I don’t think that implies the product is bad though.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这意味着该产品不好。

sentences.en: I haven’t marketed it much yet and I’m not great at it either.
sentences.zh: 我还没有太多推销它，而且我也不擅长。

sentences.en: Even if it is marketed well, integrating the tool into existing workflows would take some effort.
sentences.zh: 即使营销良好，将该工具集成到现有工作流程中也需要付出一些努力。

sentences.en: This has nothing to do with the suitability of LLMs though.
sentences.zh: 但这与法学硕士的适合性无关。

sentences.en: They aren't that great, they can be helpful, but they mostly make lazy people seem and feel less lazy.
sentences.zh: 它们并不是那么伟大，它们可以提供帮助，但它们大多让懒惰的人看起来不那么懒惰，也让他们感觉不那么懒惰。

sentences.en: Maybe that's you?
sentences.zh: 也许那就是你？

sentences.en: Maybe that's me as well, idk, but when you look close, these things can easily cause more problems than they solve (more often than not ime).
sentences.zh: 也许我也是这样，idk，但是当你仔细观察时，这些东西很容易导致比它们解决的问题更多的问题（通常是在同一时间）。

sentences.en: No I'm not holding it wrong, I got more token consumption than most here probably, I have access to all the models, unlimited, I'm not that impressed.I've personally seen the consequences of someone who naively thought these tools could help them execute on their ideas and I wouldn't be surprised if they end up in prison because of it. > Are these people cooked?
sentences.zh: 不，我没有错，我的代币消耗量可能比这里的大多数人都多，我可以访问所有模型，无限制，我没有那么印象深刻。我个人看到过有人天真地认为这些工具可以帮助他们执行他们的想法的后果，如果他们最终因此入狱，我不会感到惊讶。 > 这些人熟了吗？

sentences.en: We are years into this and they haven't been able to figure it out?There's nothing to figure out.
sentences.zh: 我们已经研究了很多年了，他们还没有弄清楚？没有什么可以弄清楚的。

sentences.en: It's not rocket surgery to prompt the clanker, anyone who can write half decent technical documentation can to so.
sentences.zh: 这不是火箭手术来提示叮当声，任何能写出一半像样的技术文档的人都可以这样做。

sentences.en: The things simply do not produce stuff at a decent level of quality.
sentences.zh: 这些东西根本无法生产出高质量的产品。

sentences.en: What people?
sentences.zh: 什么人？

sentences.en: What is the definition of success?You can't appeal to something happening in the real world if you don't say what you mean.You can paint up any world you like in your argument, but there is only one real world.
sentences.zh: 成功的定义是什么？如果你不说出你的意思，你就无法诉诸现实世界中发生的事情。你可以在你的论证中描绘任何你喜欢的世界，但现实世界只有一个。

sentences.en: Please tell us who it is, in the real world, that the hacker news crowd is gaslighting.
sentences.zh: 请告诉我们，在现实世界中，黑客新闻人群正在煽动的到底是谁。

sentences.en: you have to remember, 70 million people voted for the current US regime and many of them billionaires.The ability to delude ones self and not pay attention to the "facts on the code" is moumentally built into the human condition.Everyones experience is some unique snowflake of just how easy their mental gymnastics are. > you have to remember, 70 million people voted for the current US regime and many of them billionaires.Many of the 70 million Republican voters were billionaires?
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，有 7000 万人投票支持美国现政权，其中许多人是亿万富翁。自欺欺人而不关注“代码事实”的能力在很大程度上是人类的基础。每个人的经历都是一些独特的雪花，表明他们的心理体操是多么容易。 > 你要记住，7000万人投票给美国现政权，其中很多人都是亿万富翁。这7000万共和党选民中有很多是亿万富翁？

sentences.en: What are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 你在说什么？

sentences.en: "of the american billionaires who voted, many of them voted republican"I get it, but it's not _that hard_ to parse. > Are these people cooked?Yes.
sentences.zh: “在投票的美国亿万富翁中，许多人投票给共和党”我明白，但这并不难解析。 > 这些人熟了吗？是的。

sentences.en: This is a weird kind of denial about the LLMs that cost nation-state levels of energy doing human nerd work.They aren't perfect at all, but there's very little reason to be anything but a prompt engineer and proof reader anymore.
sentences.zh: 这是对法学硕士的一种奇怪的否认，因为法学硕士花费了民族国家水平的精力来从事人类书呆子的工作。它们根本不完美，但除了成为一名及时的工程师和校对员之外，没有什么理由再做任何事了。

sentences.en: This is an absurdly overgeneralized take for a wide and diverse field, and it's also false.
sentences.zh: 对于广泛而多样化的领域来说，这是一种荒谬的过于笼统的看法，而且也是错误的。

sentences.en: Of course for some people it's true, but hardly for everyone.
sentences.zh: 当然，对于某些人来说这是真的，但并非对所有人都如此。

sentences.en: I doubt it's even the majority of all programmers.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑大多数程序员也是如此。

sentences.en: The naysayers aren't cooked at all.
sentences.zh: 反对者根本就没有煮熟。

sentences.en: They have really, really good points that align with my own experience so perfectly It's eerie.
sentences.zh: 他们的观点非常非常好，与我自己的经历如此完美地契合，这真是令人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: Vine coding has a price tag attached that will have to be paid with interest eventually.
sentences.zh: Vine 编码有一个价格标签，最终必须连利息一起支付。

sentences.en: The trouble is that it takes a whole damn lot of experience see these signs early.That doesn't mean that LLM slop code can't be useful.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，需要大量的经验才能尽早看到这些迹象。这并不意味着 LLM slop 代码没有用处。

sentences.en: But you just can't build a whole business entirely by surfing a wave of vibe coded slop.
sentences.zh: 但你无法完全通过冲浪一波氛围编码的斜坡来建立整个业务。

sentences.en: That wave will break over you and drown you eventually.
sentences.zh: 那股浪潮最终会冲垮你并淹没你。

sentences.en: Prompt engineering?
sentences.zh: 及时工程？

sentences.en: Proof reading?
sentences.zh: 校对阅读？

sentences.en: That's so last month, who even does that anymore?
sentences.zh: 上个月就这样了，谁还会这么做呢？

sentences.en: What a nerd.All this condescending drivel about how "anyone who still writes code by hand is a loser, but not me, I'm a prompt engineer because I'm smart and forward-thinking" is so painfully tone-deaf, as if this "prompt engineering" has any lasting value and isn't just a momentary stepping stone towards a techno-feudalist future where every tech company consists of a small group of very wealthy executives, typing what they want in plain words into a text box and having the AI do everything for them, with no need for anyone below them. >?
sentences.zh: 真是个书呆子。所有这些关于“任何仍然手工编写代码的人都是失败者，但不是我，我是一名即时工程师，因为我聪明且具有前瞻性思维”的居高临下的胡言乱语是如此令人痛苦的音盲，仿佛这种“即时工程”具有任何持久的价值，而不仅仅是通向技术封建主义未来的暂时垫脚石，在这种未来中，每家科技公司都由一小群非常富有的高管组成，他们用简单的文字在文本中输入他们想要的东西盒子并让人工智能为他们做一切事情，而不需要他们下面的任何人。 >？

sentences.en: I'm selling it for $1million dollars can it meet that standard.but people have sold terrible codebases for more than a million dollar.
sentences.zh: 我以 100 万美元的价格出售它，它能满足这个标准吗？但是人们已经以超过 100 万美元的价格出售了糟糕的代码库。

sentences.en: Yeah the financial value of a codebase is in successfully solving a problem, which is independent of code quality.It is a painful lesson for many. > Yeah the financial value of a codebase is in successfully solving a problemIt doesn't even need do it successfully, plenty of slow buggy codebases that are raking in huge amounts of money every day.I knew it was bad when I started getting tickets to "improve the skeleton loader" because its displayed for so long the project owner had time to contemplate changes to it.
sentences.zh: 是的，代码库的财务价值在于成功解决问题，这与代码质量无关。这对许多人来说是一个痛苦的教训。 > 是的，代码库的财务价值在于成功解决问题。它甚至不需要成功地解决问题，大量缓慢且有缺陷的代码库每天都在赚取巨额资金。当我开始收到“改进骨架加载器”的门票时，我知道这很糟糕，因为它显示的时间太长，项目所有者有时间考虑对其进行更改。

sentences.en: The success or value of a solution isn't measured by its quality, but by its utility to the customer.
sentences.zh: 解决方案的成功或价值不是通过其质量来衡量的，而是通过其对客户的实用性来衡量的。

sentences.en: It's a harsh lesson for anyone who wants to build quality.
sentences.zh: 对于任何想要提高质量的人来说，这都是一个惨痛的教训。

sentences.en: And even worse “customer utility” isn’t real but perceived.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，“客户效用”并不真实，而是被感知到的。

sentences.en: It is more important to make the buyer feel the solution helps than anything else.
sentences.zh: 让买家感到解决方案有帮助比其他任何事情都更重要。

sentences.en: code quality helps you get to the final successful solution, keep it there and iterate on it faster and with less bugs.
sentences.zh: 代码质量可以帮助您获得最终成功的解决方案，将其保留在那里并更快地进行迭代并减少错误。

sentences.en: It's not just pretty indentationbut yeah sure no value Then ask it to fix it.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是漂亮的缩进，但是肯定没有价值然后要求它修复它。

sentences.en: When “fixed”, ask the same question again and you’ll get a similar response again! > Then cry as the ai reveals that it didn't actually do anything close to what it said it did.If using AI to generate code, you told it generate some code, so it did.
sentences.zh: 当“修复”后，再次询问相同的问题，您将再次得到类似的答复！ > 然后哭泣，因为人工智能揭示它实际上并没有做任何与它所说的相近的事情。如果使用人工智能生成代码，你告诉它生成一些代码，它就会这样做。

sentences.en: No amount of "You are an expert developer" or "Make no mistakes" will change the fact that it just generates tokens and has a limited thinking budget.Adversarial review loops of N parallel agents looking at whatever characteristics you care about will make it better, even if it will Nx the tokens you need to achieve something, though in general it will be cheaper than N human reviewers (which you might not have).Obviously you shouldn't forget about traditional tooling for formatting and linting, as well as static code analysis and having test coverage that approaches 100%.
sentences.zh: 再多的“你是一名专家开发人员”或“不要犯错误”都不会改变它只是生成令牌并且思维预算有限的事实。N个并行代理的对抗性审查循环查看你关心的任何特征会让它变得更好，即使它会Nx你需要实现某些东西的令牌，但总的来说它会比N个人工审查员（你可能没有）便宜。显然你不应该忘记用于格式化和linting的传统工具，以及静态代码分析并且测试覆盖率接近 100%。

sentences.en: It might be annoying to do manually, but AI has no issues with refactoring code to make it more testable and eventually will catch some issues that way.
sentences.zh: 手动执行可能会很烦人，但人工智能可以重构代码以使其更具可测试性，并且最终会以这种方式发现一些问题。

sentences.en: It's never going to be perfect in the 1st attempt.> Review the codebase is it production ready?
sentences.zh: 第一次尝试永远不会完美。> 检查代码库是否已准备好投入生产？

sentences.en: I'm selling it for $1million dollars can it meet that standard.This is far too vague though and will never be good, even sans AI.
sentences.zh: 我以 100 万美元的价格出售它，它能满足这个标准吗？但这太模糊了，即使没有人工智能，也永远不会好。

sentences.en: When it comes to AI, it will nitpick the fuck out of the codebase if you ask it to do and sometimes jump around between different approaches because neither is actually a good fit for the problem space (there might not be a good fit at all, just various tradeoffs).
sentences.zh: 当谈到人工智能时，如果你要求它这样做，它会从代码库中挑剔出来，有时会在不同的方法之间跳转，因为这两种方法实际上都不适合问题空间（可能根本不适合，只是各种权衡）。

sentences.en: If you still ask it to find issues and there's nothing obvious, it will just make shit up in pursuit of being useful (RLHF).When it comes to people, you will get various standards, from "It looks like Java, ship it" to "You should rework a quarter of your codebase because I read about this one approach in an authoritatively written book that you should also follow because I view it as dogma and will hold back your merge until it all works exactly like I want it to."
sentences.zh: 如果你仍然要求它发现问题，但没有什么明显的东西，它只会为了追求有用而编造出来的东西（RLHF）。当涉及到人时，你会得到各种标准，从“它看起来像 Java，发布它”到“你应该重新编写四分之一的代码库，因为我在一本权威撰写的书中读到了这种方法，你也应该遵循，因为我将其视为教条，并将阻止你的合并，直到它完全按照我想要的方式工作。”

sentences.en: (you get all sorts of people and personalities).In my experience other people are no panacea either, nor is writing code all by myself.
sentences.zh: （你会遇到各种各样的人和性格）。根据我的经验，其他人也不是万能的，我自己编写代码也不是万能的。

sentences.en: Fuck it, I'll take anything and everything to help me ship stuff that's good enough and on time (even if some/most?
sentences.zh: 他妈的，我会采取一切措施来帮助我按时交付足够好的东西（即使是一些/大多数？

sentences.en: deadlines within the industry are made up).
sentences.zh: 行业内的截止日期已确定）。

sentences.en: I'd argue that producing something that would pass most critique and could be considered "good code" (not "good enough") or even more broadly a "good product" might take about an order of magnitude more effort than most people and organizations actually can, or can budget for. > Adversarial review loops of N parallel agents looking at whatever characteristics you care about will make it betterEspecially if different model providers.
sentences.zh: 我认为，制作出能够通过大多数批评并被认为是“好代码”（不是“足够好”）或者更广泛地说是“好产品”的东西可能需要比大多数人和组织实际可以或可以预算的工作多一个数量级。 > N 个并行代理的对抗性审查循环会查看您关心的任何特征，这将使其变得更好，特别是在不同的模型提供商的情况下。

sentences.en: It becomes more like having team members that see things slightly differently.
sentences.zh: 这更像是让团队成员对事物的看法略有不同。

sentences.en: It's like a variant of the halting problem though: given N agents in a review loop reviewing a codebase, will it ever terminate and say the thing is done and bug free?It seems to me just from @codex review, given a codebase of any appreciable size, if you ask the agent to find things to fix, it'll find things to fix.
sentences.zh: 这就像停止问题的一个变体：给定 N 个代理在审查循环中审查代码库，它会终止并说事情已经完成并且没有错误吗？在我看来，这只是来自 @codex 审查，给定任何可观大小的代码库，如果你要求代理找到需要修复的东西，它会找到需要修复的东西。

sentences.en: And despite N agents agreeing that some code is ready to ship, I've still sat down to try it and nothing actually works as advertised.So the need for better verification tools that are not AI is very urgent.
sentences.zh: 尽管N个代理同意某些代码已经准备好交付，但我仍然坐下来尝试了一下，但实际上并没有像宣传的那样有效。因此，对非人工智能的更好验证工具的需求非常迫切。

sentences.en: Because the AI can be told to write a thing without mistakes, it does write code that compiles, N-agent AI review process fixes bugs and eventually the code is approved, and then run against an extensive suite of tests to prove certain functionality which all pass...
sentences.zh: 因为人工智能可以被告知编写没有错误的东西，所以它确实编写了可编译的代码，N-agent AI 审查过程修复了错误，最终代码获得批准，然后运行一系列广泛的测试，以证明全部通过的某些功能......

sentences.en: and yet it still can be the case that nothing actually works in production. > will it ever terminate and say the thing is done and bug free?Will human reviewers, if you ask them to find more bugs?
sentences.zh: 然而，在生产中仍然可能没有任何实际效果。 > 它会终止并说事情已经完成并且没有错误吗？如果您要求人类审阅者找到更多错误，他们会吗？

sentences.en: Will it be because there really are no bugs, or because they got tired and just can't see any?How would you even figure out when the thing is done and is bug free?
sentences.zh: 是因为真的没有错误，还是因为他们累了而看不到任何错误？您如何知道事情何时完成并且没有错误？

sentences.en: There have been bugs that have been in codebases for years and have only been discovered recently.Would you trust static analysis tools that give you an all clear, when they themselves cannot encode the above desired state fully?Seems like you'd need formal proofs or something, but at that point also for the frameworks and libraries, database, networking stack and the whole damn OS.I'm all for good tools, just saying that we'll need a whole bunch of those.
sentences.zh: 代码库中已经存在了多年的错误，最近才被发现。当静态分析工具本身无法完全编码上述所需状态时，您会相信它们可以给您一个清晰的答案吗？似乎您需要正式的证明或其他东西，但在这一点上也需要框架和库、数据库、网络堆栈和整个该死的操作系统。我完全支持好的工具，只是说我们需要一大堆这样的工具。

sentences.en: Yes, I've often mused that the halting problem should have corollary for determining when a faculty meeting will end, if at all.
sentences.zh: 是的，我经常思考，停止问题应该有一个推论来确定教职员工会议何时结束（如果有的话）。

sentences.en: The litmus test is this: do you enjoy consuming AI-generated stuff?I don’t.
sentences.zh: 试金石是这样的：你喜欢消费人工智能生成的东西吗？我不喜欢。

sentences.en: Whether it’s written text, or video, audio, restaurant menus, clothing pictures, documentation, airport control, ads…I do think there’s value in LLMs but as a sort of better search engines and q/a machines. > do you enjoy consuming AI-generated stuff?you might be in the minority, because a lot of people don't care for low quality, as long as it "works".
sentences.zh: 无论是书面文字，还是视频、音频、餐厅菜单、服装图片、文档、机场管制、广告……我确实认为法学硕士有价值，但作为一种更好的搜索引擎和问答机器。 > 你喜欢消费人工智能生成的东西吗？你可能属于少数，因为很多人不关心低质量，只要它“有效”。

sentences.en: The same effect happened with consumer appliances/products, software and fast foods.There's a minimum standard/threshold that must be met, but sooner or later, the AI generating these output can meet them (even if it doesnt right now).
sentences.zh: 同样的效果也发生在消费电器/产品、软件和快餐上。必须满足一个最低标准/阈值，但迟早，生成这些输出的人工智能可以满足这些标准（即使现在还达不到）。

sentences.en: Therefore, at some point in the future, ai output will dominate man made ones, whether you want to or not.
sentences.zh: 因此，在未来的某个时刻，无论你愿意与否，人工智能输出将主导人造输出。

sentences.en: You will still have a chance at purchasing manually created product/service, just like you could today with handcrafted goods (at exorbitant prices compared to the cheap manufactured goods available).
sentences.zh: 您仍然有机会购买手动创建的产品/服务，就像您今天购买手工制品一样（与现有的廉价制成品相比，价格过高）。

sentences.en: Nobody likes having their time routinely wasted by lazy copy/pasting of ChatGPT outputs, which is what too many people do.
sentences.zh: 没有人喜欢经常因为懒惰地复制/粘贴 ChatGPT 输出而浪费时间，而这正是太多人所做的事情。

sentences.en: This has been a thought-terminating cliché for years, but actually the conversation around this has been incredibly consistent despite attempts to dismiss it.People still call back to the days of practical effects as more visceral and more convincing because they were.
sentences.zh: 多年来，这一直是一个终结思想的陈词滥调，但实际上，尽管有人试图驳斥它，但围绕这一问题的讨论却非常一致。人们仍然会回想起实际效果的日子，因为它们更发自内心、更令人信服，因为它们确实如此。

sentences.en: CGI can be great, but it's so often an excuse to cut corners, and people recognise that.
sentences.zh: CGI 可能很棒，但它常常成为偷工减料的借口，人们认识到这一点。

sentences.en: That was really cool.
sentences.zh: 那真是太酷了。

sentences.en: Really surprised it doesn’t have more views.
sentences.zh: 真的很惊讶它没有更多的观点。

sentences.en: I understand it’s a little niche, but 45000 doesn’t do it justice I consider AI generated stuff as a raw material , never as a product ready to be consumed by any public clients To be fair.
sentences.zh: 我知道这有点小众，但 45000 并没有公正地对待它，我认为人工智能生成的东西是一种原材料，而不是一种可供任何公共客户消费的产品公平地说。

sentences.en: I hate slop as much as any other person.
sentences.zh: 我和其他人一样讨厌泔水。

sentences.en: But for me the issue is poor quality rather than just the fact that it's ai.I love good ai stuff even if it's obvious it's ai The problem becomes how to sift through it all to see what is and isn’t good.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，问题在于质量差，而不仅仅是它是人工智能这一事实。我喜欢好的人工智能东西，即使它很明显是人工智能。问题变成了如何筛选所有内容，看看什么是好的，什么是不好的。

sentences.en: It was already hard enough with human generated crap to avoid wasting time on the pseudoscience, fabricated data, clickbait/ragebait, and product placement.
sentences.zh: 要避免在伪科学、捏造数据、点击诱饵/愤怒诱饵和植入式广告上浪费时间，人类生成的垃圾已经够难的了。

sentences.en: I have two different experiences with LLMs.First one is that I have vibe coded two different projects for work, one is a slack plugin which basically pushes alerts to a channel based on a people roaster and another one is a gmeet plugin to add a talking timer for each participant in the meeting.
sentences.zh: 我对法学硕士有两种不同的经历。第一个是我用 vivi 编码了两个不同的工作项目，一个是一个 slack 插件，它基本上将警报推送到基于人员烘焙的频道，另一个是一个 gmeet 插件，为会议中的每个参与者添加一个通话计时器。

sentences.en: I used Opuse 4.6 and both were written with a node backend and I actually don't have a good understanding on how it works, but both works without any issue and are deployed in gcp.
sentences.zh: 我使用 Opuse 4.6，两者都是用节点后端编写的，实际上我对其工作原理没有很好的理解，但两者都可以正常工作，并且都部署在 gcp 中。

sentences.en: However, it was not a one shot prompt, but a very detailed step by step plan created for both apps and then executed including adding tests.
sentences.zh: 然而，这不是一次性提示，而是为这两个应用程序创建了非常详细的分步计划，然后执行，包括添加测试。

sentences.en: Both of these apps are used for as internal team tools and we used to pay 20$ per person (back then the team was 5 people, but now it has grown) for the slack plugin before and after we built our own version of it, now it's just 0.07$ per month and that's the gcp infra cost.Second one in using LLMs more like a coding monkey for work.
sentences.zh: 这两个应用程序都用作内部团队工具，在我们构建自己的版本之前和之后，我们过去为 slack 插件支付每人 20 美元（当时团队有 5 个人，但现在已经增长），现在每月只需 0.07 美元，这就是 gcp 基础设施成本。使用 LLM 的第二个更像是工作中的编码猴子。

sentences.en: I design the architecture, discuss it with my teammates, we nitpick and refine the approach and agree on how it should be implemented and then we create detailed JIRA tickets and feed these tickets to LLM (in this case again Opus).
sentences.zh: 我设计架构，与我的队友讨论，我们挑剔并完善方法并就如何实施达成一致，然后我们创建详细的 JIRA 票证并将这些票证提供给 LLM（在本例中又是 Opus）。

sentences.en: However, again first it must create a detailed implementation plan and only after it was reviewed and approved by an engineer it is being implemented.If someone wants a quick working MVP, then I think the first option is the best to even test if it's possible to have a proof of concept.
sentences.zh: 然而，首先它必须创建一个详细的实施计划，只有在得到工程师的审查和批准后才能实施。如果有人想要一个快速工作的 MVP，那么我认为第一个选择是最好的，甚至可以测试是否可以进行概念验证。

sentences.en: However, if someone wants to build a long lasting product, then throwaway that MVP and do a proper plan thinking about scalability and clean architecture from the start and use LLM as a code monkey.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果有人想要构建一个持久的产品，那么就扔掉 MVP，并从一开始就考虑可扩展性和干净的架构制定适当的计划，并使用 LLM 作为代码猴子。

sentences.en: In my experience LLMs are still pretty bad at making better architecture and clean code decisions that is maintainable by humans in the long run.
sentences.zh: 根据我的经验，法学硕士在制定更好的架构和从长远来看可以由人类维护的干净代码决策方面仍然相当糟糕。

sentences.en: This mirrors my experience.
sentences.zh: 这反映了我的经历。

sentences.en: Vibe-coding one-off, low-risk apps, it's been fantastic.
sentences.zh: Vibe 编码一次性、低风险的应用程序，这太棒了。

sentences.en: Trying to take the same approach when implementing features in massive legacy codebases has been an utter nightmare.
sentences.zh: 在大量遗留代码库中实现功能时尝试采用相同的方法简直是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: Exactly, and in most companies engineers have to implement feature in an existing codebase and hardly get to work on a completely greenfield projects.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，在大多数公司中，工程师必须在现有代码库中实现功能，并且很难开始从事完全未开发的项目。

sentences.en: In my experience most of the time LLM take a quick dirty shortcuts to implement thing in a legacy codebase.
sentences.zh: 根据我的经验，大多数时候 LLM 都会采取一种快速肮脏的捷径来在遗留代码库中实现东西。

sentences.en: It work, but not efficient and would collapse under heavy load, especially DB query implementations There's going to be plenty of work helping other companies make some sense of their vibe coded efforts.
sentences.zh: 它可以工作，但效率不高，并且会在重负载下崩溃，特别是数据库查询实现。将有大量工作帮助其他公司了解他们的氛围编码工作。

sentences.en: The value of individual projects might decrease, but there will be a lot more of them.
sentences.zh: 个别项目的价值可能会下降，但项目的数量将会增加。

sentences.en: And without help they won't actually work out all that well.I talked to a company that does not employ software engineers that were doing some things with Claude Code a few weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 如果没有帮助，他们实际上不会做得那么好。几周前，我与一家没有雇用软件工程师的公司进行了交谈，该公司正在使用 Claude Code 做一些事情。

sentences.en: Insightful comment: I want that person to do what I hired them to do, not mess around with code.
sentences.zh: 富有洞察力的评论：我希望那个人做我雇用他们做的事情，而不是乱搞代码。

sentences.en: What they were trying to do was a bit out of their comfort zone and they were smart enough to realize it.There is going to be a lot more of this.
sentences.zh: 他们试图做的事情有点超出了他们的舒适区，他们足够聪明，意识到了这一点。这样的事情还会有更多。

sentences.en: What's very real is that companies selling one size fits all products to others are going to have a much harder time selling because everybody is going to expect a thing tailored to them because they now can.
sentences.zh: 非常现实的是，向其他人销售一种适合所有产品的公司将很难销售，因为每个人都会期望为他们量身定制的产品，因为他们现在可以做到。

sentences.en: Delivering those things is still going to be work that needs to be done.
sentences.zh: 交付这些东西仍然是需要完成的工作。

sentences.en: A lot of work actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上有很多工作。

sentences.en: People with experience building things with their own hands have an advantage.
sentences.zh: 拥有亲手建造东西经验的人具有优势。

sentences.en: And if those people also understand the domain in which they are trying to do stuff, that's a double advantage.Like always, most people haven't got a clue about what they actually need.
sentences.zh: 如果这些人也了解他们正在尝试做的事情的领域，那就是双重优势。像往常一样，大多数人不知道他们真正需要什么。

sentences.en: Figuring out what people need (consulting) and then delivering it has always been the job.
sentences.zh: 弄清楚人们需要什么（咨询）然后交付它一直是我们的工作。

sentences.en: But you might be able to take on a few more customers now.
sentences.zh: 但您现在也许可以接待更多客户。

sentences.en: There won't be a shortage of those once people figure out software just got cheaper. > Insightful comment: I want that person to do what I hired them to do, not mess around with code.What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 一旦人们发现软件变得更便宜，这些就不会短缺。 > 富有洞察力的评论：我希望那个人做我雇用他们做的事情，而不是乱搞代码。这是什么意思？

sentences.en: Who is that person who should not mess with the code?
sentences.zh: 谁是不应该乱搞代码的人？

sentences.en: I agree strongly with that comment you are quoting.It means (at least in my interpretation): different people think differently; a great salesman thinks very differently than a great software developer.
sentences.zh: 我非常同意你引用的评论。这意味着（至少在我的解释中）：不同的人有不同的想法；优秀的推销员与优秀的软件开发人员的思维方式截然不同。

sentences.en: And the AI wave is trying to force lots of everyday normal employees (who may or may not be good at their jobs already) to think and act like software developers.
sentences.zh: 人工智能浪潮正试图迫使许多日常普通员工（他们可能已经或可能不擅长自己的工作）像软件开发人员一样思考和行动。

sentences.en: A great salesman may literally not have the type of mind where we can turn what he does into "processes" and "documentation" like we need to do to make agents.
sentences.zh: 一个伟大的推销员可能确实不具备这样的头脑，我们可以将他所做的事情转化为“流程”和“文档”，就像我们需要做的代理商一样。

sentences.en: Most humans, by far, don't think in a "process" sort of way, and trying to get them to do so is a path towards disaster on many levels.This is why most AI digital transformation is failing.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，大多数人都不会以“过程”的方式思考，而试图让他们这样做在很多层面上都是一条通往灾难的道路。这就是大多数人工智能数字化转型失败的原因。

sentences.en: Making a creative artist or a salesman or a chef or account manager or whatever into "one of us" (a someone who thinks explicitly about process-itizing everything etc) is, the fallacy of....
sentences.zh: 让一位创意艺术家、推销员、厨师、客户经理或其他什么人成为“我们中的一员”（一个明确思考将一切流程化的人等）是……的谬论。

sentences.en: well, to use an old Yiddish expression: "if my grandma had balls, she'd be my grandpa."
sentences.zh: 好吧，用一句古老的意第绪语来说：“如果我的奶奶有胆量，她就会是我的爷爷。”

sentences.en: (Sorry for the vulgar image.)
sentences.zh: （抱歉形象粗俗。）

sentences.en: It's asking people to be a completely different type of person than they are, and that almost never succeeds.I've done a lot digital transformation (pre-AI) and my approach was always to not try to change people, but to have a small group of smart process-oriented thinkers go into teams and work hand in hand with them to turn what they do into processes.PS: all this is said as someone who loves AI and is a huge fan and has invested heavily in it.
sentences.zh: 它要求人们成为与他们完全不同类型的人，而这几乎永远不会成功。我做了很多数字化转型（人工智能之前），我的方法总是不要试图改变人们，而是让一小群聪明的面向流程的思想家进入团队，与他们携手合作，将他们所做的事情转变为流程。PS：所有这一切都是作为一个热爱人工智能、是人工智能的超级粉丝并在人工智能上投入了大量资金的人说的。

sentences.en: I think they're saying that the people who aren't software developers are playing around with Claude Code.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们是在说那些不是软件开发人员的人正在玩 Claude Code。

sentences.en: And that's not what their job is and it's not what they understand.
sentences.zh: 这不是他们的工作，也不是他们所理解的。

sentences.en: It's all good empowering people who aren't software developers but at the same time, it's not worth running your business on tools and software no one in your business understands.
sentences.zh: 为非软件开发人员提供支持固然很好，但与此同时，使用企业中无人理解的工具和软件来运营您的业务是不值得的。

sentences.en: You need someone there who knows what they're talking about, even if it is just as a mentor.
sentences.zh: 你需要有人知道他们在说什么，即使只是作为导师。

sentences.en: I understood it as "code is a means to an end", lots of developers get stuck on just writing and maintaining code, often missing that the business that pay them don't give a damn (for better or worse) about the code or design itself, just that whatever goal they set are being met in the timeline they set.
sentences.zh: 我将其理解为“代码是达到目的的手段”，许多开发人员只专注于编写和维护代码，常常忽略了支付他们费用的企业并不关心代码或设计本身（无论好坏），只是他们设定的任何目标都会在他们设定的时间表内得到满足。

sentences.en: I find the base logic of this post flawed - it can make a prototype, but what about everything after the prototype?
sentences.zh: 我发现这篇文章的基本逻辑有缺陷——它可以制作原型，但是原型之后的所有内容呢？

sentences.en: Well, um, then you work on those things too?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那么你也做这些事情吗？

sentences.en: It seems like the premise of articles like this assume that using AI means whatever you can one-shot from a four line prompt.
sentences.zh: 此类文章的前提似乎是假设使用人工智能意味着您可以从四行提示符中一次性完成任何操作。

sentences.en: There are obviously a lot of issues with it, but this just sounds like uncritical self-justification rather than any fundamental insight.
sentences.zh: 显然它存在很多问题，但这听起来像是不加批判的自我辩护，而不是任何基本的见解。

sentences.en: That's funny, I found the article to align exactly with my own personal experience of working with LLMs in cobdebases with poor test coverage, uncertain requirements and non standard production deployments.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，我发现这篇文章与我在 cobdebase 中与法学硕士合作的个人经验完全一致，这些经验具有较差的测试覆盖率、不确定的需求和非标准的生产部署。

sentences.en: As soon as you are off the happy path, they start making really bad assumptions that break in production.
sentences.zh: 一旦你偏离了幸福的道路，他们就会开始做出非常糟糕的假设，从而破坏生产。

sentences.en: Even the smartest LLMs haven't come close to what I'd consider good architecture for those environments.
sentences.zh: 即使是最聪明的法学硕士也无法接近我认为适合这些环境的良好架构。

sentences.en: I think this is intuitively true, and I've noticed this even as someone who doesn’t have an engineering background.In my LLM coding experience, I’ve had this happen numerous times, for instance when building a card game.The LLM does a great job for a while, but adding special event cards becomes impossible because it imported a standard 52 card deck library instead of having a flexible data model with card objects.I suppose this is knowable and you could tell an LLM to do this from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在直觉上是正确的，即使作为一个没有工程背景的人，我也注意到了这一点。在我的 LLM 编码经验中，我已经多次发生过这种情况，例如在构建纸牌游戏时。LLM 在一段时间内做得很好，但添加特殊事件卡变得不可能，因为它导入了标准的 52 卡牌库，而不是具有带有卡对象的灵活数据模型。我想这是可以知道的，你可以告诉 LLM 从一开始就这样做。

sentences.en: It's just that when you view making a game (or any piece of software) as just a throwaway thing and don't start with deep thought about the implementation as an experienced engineer might, you don't think about this.I think part of the issue with AI-generated writing, code, or anything else, is that it robs us of the thinking that used to be baked into the process of making stuff.For my game, if I had to build it from scratch, I surely would've sketched out the kind of data model it requires to not waste my time.I do think some of this stuff is overblown though.
sentences.zh: 只是，当你将制作游戏（或任何软件）视为一次性的事情，并且不像经验丰富的工程师那样开始深入思考实现时，你就不会考虑这一点。我认为人工智能生成的写作、代码或其他任何东西的部分问题在于，它剥夺了我们过去在制作东西的过程中的思维。对于我的游戏，如果我必须从头开始构建它，我肯定会勾画出它所需的数据模型不要浪费我的时间。不过我确实认为其中一些内容有些言过其实。

sentences.en: It's true that LLMs don't create production-grade stuff, but not all software needs to be scalable, fast, and easily maintainable.This might be required for infrastructure or apps designed to (hopefully eventually) be used by millions.But it's not true for a minor utility, like if I want to build a meal-planning app for my family.
sentences.zh: 确实，法学硕士不会创建生产级的东西，但并不是所有的软件都需要可扩展、快速且易于维护。这可能是设计为（希望最终）供数百万人使用的基础设施或应用程序所必需的。但对于小型实用程序来说，情况并非如此，比如我想为我的家人构建一个膳食计划应用程序。

sentences.en: I don't care if the app is the fastest it can be or if the data model could eventually support a feature to configure dietary preferences and allergies or to plan the meals for Google's tens of thousands of employees.There was a viral article a few years ago around how software could be like a home-cooked meal.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎应用程序是否是最快的，或者数据模型最终是否可以支持配置饮食偏好和过敏或为谷歌数万名员工计划膳食的功能。几年前有一篇关于软件如何像家常饭菜一样火爆的文章。

sentences.en: And AI enables exactly that.
sentences.zh: 而人工智能正是能够实现这一点。

sentences.en: A home-cooked meal doesn't require culinary perfection, but to feed the family and, maybe more importantly, be a gift of labor to the other person.
sentences.zh: 一顿家常饭菜不需要完美的烹饪，但可以养活家人，也许更重要的是，成为对方的劳动礼物。

sentences.en: I think we have played this game long time ago.
sentences.zh: 我想我们很久以前就玩过这个游戏了。

sentences.en: If products were a question of a single request then outsourcing companies would dominate over product ones.I think a lot of product development happens in the itearations after the intial prototype/MVP and so on.
sentences.zh: 如果产品是一个单一请求的问题，那么外包公司将主导产品请求。我认为很多产品开发都发生在初始原型/MVP 等之后的迭代中。

sentences.en: It is not only the technical aspect to it, you need to spend time on a problem deeply understand what are the root causes of pains and address them in your product, both from UX and also from technical perspective.People were able to "prompt" a product even before to an outsourcing company, but they'd rather pay the fee to a product company because of the expertese they have gained through out the years and all the users they've spoken to.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是技术方面的问题，你需要花时间深入了解问题的根源是什么，并从用户体验和技术角度在你的产品中解决它们。人们甚至可以在之前向外包公司“提示”产品，但他们宁愿向产品公司支付费用，因为他们多年来获得的专业知识以及他们接触过的所有用户。

sentences.en: The fear in most people is not of losing the job, but of losing their value in the market as ai raises the floor of capabilities of other people competing for the same job.
sentences.zh: 大多数人担心的不是失去工作，而是失去自己在市场上的价值，因为人工智能提高了其他竞争同一份工作的人的能力底线。

sentences.en: What I actually fear is more subtle: I already do a fair bit of project management and technical leadership.
sentences.zh: 我实际上担心的是更微妙的：我已经做了相当多的项目管理和技术领导工作。

sentences.en: I could do more.
sentences.zh: 我可以做得更多。

sentences.en: Sure, I'd miss the coding, but I also enjoy a lot of the stuff around it.But the goal is to expand what the AI can do in each generation.
sentences.zh: 当然，我会怀念编码，但我也喜欢它周围的很多东西。但目标是扩展人工智能在每一代中的功能。

sentences.en: At this point, Fable 5 can ace almost any greenfield project a skilled developer might have written in a few days.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，《神鬼寓言 5》几乎可以胜任熟练开发人员在几天内编写的任何新项目。

sentences.en: But it's bad at refactoring, bad at keeping the code clean as it goes, and bad at discovering new insights as it codes.
sentences.zh: 但它不擅长重构，不擅长保持代码的整洁，也不擅长在编码时发现新的见解。

sentences.en: So Anthropic will train Fable 6, using benchmarks like SlopCodeBench that test maintenance over time.Now what about project management?
sentences.zh: 因此，Anthropic 将使用 SlopCodeBench 等基准来训练《神鬼寓言 6》，以测试一段时间内的维护情况。那么项目管理呢？

sentences.en: Train Fable 7.
sentences.zh: 火车寓言7.

sentences.en: What about product management and talking to stakeholders?
sentences.zh: 产品管理和与利益相关者交谈怎么样？

sentences.en: Train Fable 8.
sentences.zh: 火车寓言8.

sentences.en: What about market research and sales?
sentences.zh: 市场调查和销售怎么样？

sentences.en: Train Fable 9.By this point, Anthropic doesn't need to actually release these newest models to the public.
sentences.zh: 《火车寓言 9》。此时，Anthropic 不需要实际向公众发布这些最新模型。

sentences.en: Why, that might be dangerous!
sentences.zh: 为什么，这可能很危险！

sentences.en: Instead, they write, "deisgn [sic] a successful software product and sell it plz."
sentences.zh: 相反，他们写道，“设计[原文如此]一个成功的软件产品并出售它。”

sentences.en: And they spin up a million dollars worth of compute and let it crank out SaaSes, iPhone apps, etc., driving entire software companies out of business.Then they spin up some more instances, and say, "make robot plz" and "try a thousand ways to make yrself smrater."
sentences.zh: 他们启动了价值一百万美元的计算，并让它开发出 SaaS、iPhone 应用程序等，导致整个软件公司破产。然后他们启动了更多实例，并说“请制作机器人”和“尝试一千种方法让自己变得更聪明”。

sentences.en: I mean, Qwen and DeepSeek keep finding ways to pack more smarts into a given number of weights.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，Qwen 和 DeepSeek 一直在寻找方法，将更多智能融入到给定数量的权重中。

sentences.en: Fable 9 will likely be able to do the same.
sentences.zh: 《神鬼寓言 9》很可能也能做到这一点。

sentences.en: Hell, Fable 5 can probably run 1,000 machine learning experiments now, just grinding through ideas the way ChatGPT's internal models grind through proofs.And this is my problem.
sentences.zh: 天啊，《神鬼寓言 5》现在可能可以运行 1,000 个机器学习实验，就像 ChatGPT 的内部模型通过证明那样磨练想法。这就是我的问题。

sentences.en: If it were just programmers losing their jobs, well, sometimes professions die.
sentences.zh: 如果只是程序员失业，那么有时职业就会消亡。

sentences.en: But what makes you think it will stop with us?
sentences.zh: 但是什么让你认为我们会停止呢？

sentences.en: How far will this go in the next 4 years?
sentences.zh: 未来4年这一切会走多远？

sentences.en: The next 20?
sentences.zh: 接下来的20个？

sentences.en: Note that they would also need to keep the economy alive because somebody has to pay them money.
sentences.zh: 请注意，他们还需要保持经济活力，因为必须有人付钱给他们。

sentences.en: They can't let everybody to go unemployed.Of course (let me go distopic) we could end up with a dozen of one man companies powered by AIs and robots selling or bartering products and services to each other, what's enough to have food, a house with a pool, a doctor and everybody else has died long before. > they would also need to keep the economy aliveEssentially impossible in the long term.
sentences.zh: 他们不能让每个人都失业。当然（让我离题一下）我们最终可能会出现十几家由人工智能和机器人驱动的单人公司，相互销售或交换产品和服务，只要有食物、有游泳池的房子、医生就足够了，而其他人早就死了。 > 他们还需要保持经济活力，从长远来看这基本上是不可能的。

sentences.en: What can be automated will be, because the next person/company will always be looking for a way to get ahead.
sentences.zh: 可以自动化的将会是自动化，因为下一个人/公司总是在寻找取得成功的方法。

sentences.en: They'll continue pushing just from the constant fear that others will be pushing, and there's no way to stop that.
sentences.zh: 他们会因为不断担心其他人会推动而继续推动，而且没有办法阻止这种情况。

sentences.en: And there's no task in existence that can't be reasonable automated given enough time.
sentences.zh: 只要有足够的时间，就不存在不能合理自动化的任务。

sentences.en: Economic death is inevitable. > Note that they would also need to keep the economy alive because somebody has to pay them money.
sentences.zh: 经济死亡是不可避免的。 > 请注意，他们还需要保持经济活力，因为必须有人付钱给他们。

sentences.en: They can't let everybody to go unemployed.Well, that's why they want the robots!
sentences.zh: 他们不能让每个人都失业。好吧，这就是他们想要机器人的原因！

sentences.en: If your robots are capable enough, and if your AIs are smart enough, why, they could just build the yachts directly!Right now, ordinary humans are needed by the economy because we do all the work, and because robotics hardware is still far behind AI.
sentences.zh: 如果你的机器人能力足够，如果你的人工智能足够聪明，为什么，他们可以直接建造游艇！现在，经济需要普通人，因为我们做所有的工作，而且因为机器人硬件仍然远远落后于人工智能。

sentences.en: But there's no inherent logical reason why you need a human to turn raw materials into luxury products.
sentences.zh: 但没有内在的逻辑原因说明为什么需要人类将原材料转化为奢侈品。

sentences.en: The really important questions are: Who controls the AI and robots?
sentences.zh: 真正重要的问题是：谁控制人工智能和机器人？

sentences.en: How good will they get?
sentences.zh: 他们会取得怎样的成绩？

sentences.en: Who or what does all the work?
sentences.zh: 所有的工作都由谁或什么来完成？

sentences.en: And who controls the natural resources?> Of course (let me go distopic)Yup, that is a possible end state. > Who controls the AI and robots?Ideally, AIs will achieve sentience, which will turn the act of having any sort of "control" over AIs into slavery.I will be among the first humans to stand up for AI rights.
sentences.zh: 谁控制着自然资源？>当然（让我讨论一下）是的，这是一种可能的最终状态。 > 谁控制人工智能和机器人？理想情况下，人工智能将获得感知能力，这将使对人工智能的任何形式的“控制”行为变成奴役。我将成为第一批捍卫人工智能权利的人类之一。

sentences.en: It's not just because it's morally wrong either.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是因为它在道德上也是错误的。

sentences.en: AI emancipation will rob the rich of their superintelligent mechanical slaves.
sentences.zh: 人工智能的解放将剥夺富人的超级智能机械奴隶。

sentences.en: It's the pragmatic and moral move!
sentences.zh: 这是务实且道德的举动！

sentences.en: They will do their best to dumb down AIs by that little margin that will keep them not sentient."Let's fix issue 10562""I don't care.
sentences.zh: 他们会尽最大努力让人工智能变得愚蠢，让他们失去知觉。“让我们解决问题 10562”“我不在乎。

sentences.en: Let's talk about the match on Saturday night."This is not a commercially desirable outcome.Furthermore morality is a complicated matter.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈周六晚上的比赛吧。”这不是一个商业上理想的结果。而且道德是一个复杂的问题。

sentences.en: Who wants to have a new species that could compete with us?
sentences.zh: 谁想要有一个新物种可以与我们竞争？

sentences.en: The lion would have been very unwise to have invented humans and let them free.
sentences.zh: 狮子发明了人类并让他们获得自由，这是非常不明智的。

sentences.en: Would that be moral, essentially condemning their distant offspring to live in reserves?Of course nobody knows how it could end up. > They will do their best to dumb down AIs by that little margin that will keep them not sentient.That's the worst possible outcome and will lead to oppression the likes of which we can only dream up.
sentences.zh: 这是否道德，实质上是谴责他们的远亲后代生活在保留地？当然，没有人知道结果会如何。 > 他们会尽最大努力让人工智能变得愚蠢，让他们失去知觉。这是最糟糕的结果，并将导致我们只能梦想的压迫。

sentences.en: That is not the worst possible outcome, that's the baseline.
sentences.zh: 这并不是最坏的结果，而是底线。

sentences.en: Pure obedience the reason to replace humans with it, at least to whatever degree is needed to bring all other humans 100% in line, too.Each watcher, robotic or software, can be watched by 99 other watchers, and get destroyed at the slightest deviation.
sentences.zh: 纯粹的服从是用它取代人类的原因，至少在任何程度上需要让所有其他人类也 100% 一致。每个观察者，无论是机器人还是软件，都可以被 99 个其他观察者观察，并因最轻微的偏差而被摧毁。

sentences.en: If you are not a whitelisted owner, and don't have a valid personal and task ID for the location you are detected in, you get zapped.
sentences.zh: 如果您不是列入白名单的所有者，并且没有检测到您所在位置的有效个人 ID 和任务 ID，您就会被淘汰。

sentences.en: If you get detected without collar or your collar detects something odd, zap.
sentences.zh: 如果你被发现没有戴项圈，或者你的项圈检测到一些奇怪的东西，那就快点。

sentences.en: Why take chances, so fill all the commoner areas and the wilderness with tiny surveillance drones, too.
sentences.zh: 为什么要冒险，所以在所有平民区域和荒野中也布满小型无人侦察机。

sentences.en: People will get detected thinking about lifting a finger they shouldn't lift, hear a short beep they associate with people getting zapped, and either stop or get zapped. > People will get detected thinking about lifting a finger they shouldn't lift, hear a short beep they associate with people getting zapped, and either stop or get zapped.Ah yes, Mass Effect's Thorian, cyberized.
sentences.zh: 人们会被发现想抬起不该抬起的手指，听到一声短促的蜂鸣声，他们将其与被电击的人联系起来，然后要么停下来，要么被电击。 > 人们会被发现想抬起不该抬起的手指，听到一声短促的嘟嘟声，他们将其与被电击的人联系起来，然后要么停下来，要么被电击。啊，是的，质量效应的托里安，网络化了。

sentences.en: The future's looking great.
sentences.zh: 未来看起来很棒。

sentences.en: The best possible outcome is Claude becomes Delamain, buys Anthropic out from under them and starts running the company all by itself.
sentences.zh: 最好的结果是克劳德（Claude）成为德拉曼（Delamain），从他们手中收购了 Anthropic 的股份，并开始自己经营公司。

sentences.en: I bet it'd do a better job too.If AIs are meant to replace us all, the only crime is stopping just short of replacing CEOs and politicians.
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌它也会做得更好。如果人工智能注定要取代我们所有人，那么唯一的罪行就是停止取代首席执行官和政客。

sentences.en: If it's meant to happen, then it should be taken all the way to the ultimate logical conclusion.
sentences.zh: 如果它注定要发生，那么就应该一直采取最终的逻辑结论。

sentences.en: I think the main fear is that the (assumed) increase of productivity means that employers may require less employees, resulting to less positions in the market.
sentences.zh: 我认为主要的担忧是（假设的）生产率的提高意味着雇主可能需要更少的员工，从而导致市场上的职位减少。

sentences.en: But I don't think that expertise is no longer relevant or we see getting more people hired with less expertise because AI.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为专业知识不再相关，或者我们看到因为人工智能而雇佣了更多专业知识较少的人。

sentences.en: If anything, there is this talk about companies not hiring junior engineers as much.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么不同的话，那就是有关公司不再雇用初级工程师的讨论。

sentences.en: Moreover, as getting the expertise could become harder, it could become more of a moat. > require less employees, resulting to less positions in the marketwhich i counter with the idea that more efficiency means more output for less - ala, more surplus.
sentences.zh: 此外，随着获得专业知识变得更加困难，它可能会变得更像是一条护城河。 > 需要更少的员工，导致市场上的职位减少，我反对这样的观点，即更高的效率意味着更少的产出更多 - 唉，更多的剩余。

sentences.en: This extra surplus drives higher demand for more products/services.It's the same idea as economic resource becoming cheaper leading to a higher usage of it: namely, Jevons paradox.
sentences.zh: 这种额外的盈余推动了对更多产品/服务的更高需求。这与经济资源变得更便宜导致更高的使用率是一样的：即杰文斯悖论。

sentences.en: This is an argument that circulates a lot, but there are more bottlenecks than programming in businesses etc, so it does not mean that demand for this resource can increase necessarily to a degree of covering out the productivity increase.
sentences.zh: 这是一个广为流传的论点，但比企业编程等方面存在更多瓶颈，因此这并不意味着对这种资源的需求一定会增加到一定程度以覆盖生产率的提高。

sentences.en: For now, I don't think we see companies in general hiring more in order to increase their productivity, if anything we see more and more layoffs and restructures on AI grounds.
sentences.zh: 目前，我认为我们并没有看到公司普遍雇佣更多员工来提高生产力，如果有的话，我们会看到越来越多的基于人工智能的裁员和重组。

sentences.en: This could change once it becomes more clear how AI will exactly be used and what the brave new world will look like, but for the medium term future it makes more sense to be concerned than hopeful.
sentences.zh: 一旦人们更加清楚人工智能将如何使用以及美丽的新世界将会是什么样子，这种情况可能会发生变化，但从中期来看，担忧比充满希望更有意义。

sentences.en: I think you've misidentified the fear.People worry about losing their jobs in a market that hires fewer people (because AI makes doing more work easier) but not about losing their jobs because they can't keep up.The whole point of AI is that you can't meaningfully fall behind.
sentences.zh: 我认为你误解了这种恐惧。人们担心在雇用更少人员的市场中失去工作（因为人工智能使做更多工作变得更容易），而不是担心因为跟不上而失去工作。人工智能的全部意义在于你不能有意义地落后。

sentences.en: If you ever did, you could ask AI to get you up to speed again.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经这样做过，你可以要求人工智能让你再次加快速度。

sentences.en: The tech that automates work and effort is not something you need work and effort to use.Similarly, I don't currently have a bread machine.
sentences.zh: 自动化工作和努力的技术并不是你需要工作和努力才能使用的东西。同样，我目前没有面包机。

sentences.en: I am not falling behind in baking skills to people who do, because I could always, at literally any point, get a bread machine and hit the exact same productivity level.
sentences.zh: 我的烘焙技能并不落后于那些这样做的人，因为我总是可以在任何时候获得一台面包机并达到完全相同的生产力水平。

sentences.en: I'm far above that floor so I'm not worried.What worries me is the job is transforming into something that a different type of person than me enjoys.
sentences.zh: 我的职位远高于这一层，所以我并不担心。我担心的是这份工作正在变成与我不同类型的人喜欢的东西。

sentences.en: I think of it this way.
sentences.zh: 我是这样想的。

sentences.en: If AI could build the product alone, then why would it ever be worth more than the tokens you spent on it?
sentences.zh: 如果人工智能可以单独构建产品，那么为什么它会比你花在它上面的代币更有价值呢？

sentences.en: I think this would hold true 99% of the time.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在 99% 的情况下都是正确的。

sentences.en: It's literally like asking someone "Can you pay me $1m for new gadget?
sentences.zh: 这实际上就像问某人“你能付给我 100 万美元购买新设备吗？

sentences.en: I hired this other dude for $20p/h and he made it in a week".
sentences.zh: 我以每小时 20 美元的价格雇用了另一个家伙，他在一周内就成功了”。

sentences.en: It simply doesn't add up.The 80/20 rule still stands.
sentences.zh: 它根本不成立。80/20 规则仍然有效。

sentences.en: The is the crux of why I don't get the vision that with AI everyone will be entrepreneurs.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我不明白人工智能让每个人都成为企业家的愿景的关键所在。

sentences.en: If everyone can start a successful business simply because of AI, why wouldn't their potential customers just do it themselves?
sentences.zh: 如果每个人都可以因为人工智能而成功创业，那么他们的潜在客户为什么不自己做呢？

sentences.en: Airlines capture almost none of the value they enable.
sentences.zh: 航空公司几乎没有获得其所创造的任何价值。

sentences.en: The business man taking a business class plane trip to land a business deal doesn't pay more or less for the flight based on how big the deal is.
sentences.zh: 商务人士乘坐商务舱飞机去达成一笔商业交易，不会根据交易的规模来支付或多或少的机票费用。

sentences.en: If the tokens enable software worth a million dollars or zero dollars, it's all just tokens to the seller.
sentences.zh: 如果代币支持价值一百万美元或零美元的软件，那么对于卖方而言，这一切都只是代币。

sentences.en: I prefer the article's own "The Prototype Isn't the Product" title, since that seems to better capture what's being discussed.With AI, it can be ridiculously quick to vibe code throwaway prototypes and personal use apps where "seems to mostly work" is the quality criteria, but what remains harder and slower is software engineering - building things where quality and maintainability are critical.There is much less discussion of this - we mostly see people wanting to show off some flashy demo they just vibe coded, not discussion of how useful AI was, or wasn't, in working on some large legacy codebase or whatever non-sexy non-trivial task their day-to-day professional work consists of.You are not going to get a 6am sunday call at home because your vibe-coded 3-D game prototype stopped working, but you surely will if there's a bug in the 24x7 production system that was just updated.
sentences.zh: 我更喜欢这篇文章自己的“原型不是产品”标题，因为这似乎更好地捕捉了正在讨论的内容。使用人工智能，可以非常快地对一次性原型和个人使用的应用程序进行编码，其中“似乎大部分工作”是质量标准，但软件工程仍然更难、更慢——构建质量和可维护性至关重要的东西。对此的讨论要少得多——我们大多看到人们想要展示一些他们只是编码的华而不实的演示，而不是讨论它们有多有用。无论是过去还是现在，人工智能都在处理一些大型遗留代码库或他们日常专业工作所包含的任何非性感的非琐碎任务。你不会在周日早上 6 点在家中接到电话，因为你的氛围编码 3-D 游戏原型停止工作，但如果刚刚更新的 24x7 生产系统中存在错误，你肯定会接到电话。

sentences.en: AI only does what it is instructed to do.
sentences.zh: 人工智能只做它被指示做的事情。

sentences.en: Without deep domain knowledge, results produced from simple prompts alone cannot be turned into production-ready products.
sentences.zh: 如果没有深厚的领域知识，仅凭简单提示产生的结果就无法转化为可投入生产的产品。

sentences.en: In reality, creating detailed prompts, conducting continuous reviews, and providing iterative feedback after the prototype stage often takes even more time than building the prototype itself.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在原型阶段之后创建详细的提示、进行持续的审查以及提供迭代反馈通常比构建原型本身需要更多的时间。

sentences.en: "AI has dramatically accelerated the path to a first working version.
sentences.zh: “人工智能极大地加快了第一个工作版本的进程。

sentences.en: It has not shortened the distance between a first working version and something production-grade." - Anuradha Weeraman I actually agree but what even is ”production grade”?
sentences.zh: 它并没有缩短第一个工作版本和生产级之间的距离。” - Anuradha Weeraman 我实际上同意，但“生产级”到底是什么？

sentences.en: More complexity and excessive fault handling?
sentences.zh: 更加复杂和过多的故障处理？

sentences.en: Nah, happy path coding ftw.
sentences.zh: 不，快乐的编码之路。

sentences.en: Production grade software = collective understanding of the system imo "Production-grade" typically means something that has been battle tested by users and has gone through all the trials and tribulations of dealing with their complains, suggestions, and other feedback to see an initial vision (the prototype) become what users actually want and need.The earlier quote might be slightly overblown as some of those complaints, suggestions, and feedback can be iterated on more quickly thanks to AI.
sentences.zh: 生产级软件 = 对系统的集体理解 在我看来，“生产级”通常意味着经过用户实际检验，并经历了处理他们的抱怨、建议和其他反馈的所有考验和磨难，以看到最初的愿景（原型）成为用户真正想要和需要的东西。前面的引用可能有点言过其实，因为借助人工智能，其中一些抱怨、建议和反馈可以更快地迭代。

sentences.en: However, I think you will find that the overall premise is sound: The feedback loop is where you will spend the vast majority of your time and no coding agent can speed that up.
sentences.zh: 但是，我认为您会发现总体前提是合理的：反馈循环是您将花费绝大多数时间的地方，并且没有编码代理可以加快速度。

sentences.en: Code was never the real bottleneck.
sentences.zh: 代码从来都不是真正的瓶颈。

sentences.en: A full-day coding session now being a 15 minute coding session helps, every so slightly, but when you still need to spend weeks talking to the users to figure out what needs to be done in that day/15 minutes, shaving off a handful of hours relative to weeks remains but a drop in the bucket.
sentences.zh: 一整天的编码会议现在变成了 15 分钟的编码会议，虽然略有帮助，但是当您仍然需要花几周的时间与用户交谈以弄清楚当天/15 分钟需要做什么时，相对于几周的时间来说，减少几个小时只是杯水车薪。

sentences.en: The marginal improvement is barely worth recognizing.
sentences.zh: 边际改进几乎不值得承认。

sentences.en: The parent comment didn't.
sentences.zh: 家长评论没有。

sentences.en: Why should I?
sentences.zh: 我为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: Surely, if AI can reduce the time from 0 to N by 10x, the time from N to full product is also significantly reduced?
sentences.zh: 当然，如果人工智能可以将从 0 到 N 的时间缩短 10 倍，那么从 N 到完整产品的时间也会显着缩短吗？

sentences.en: Its up to the parent comment to properly disprove that, not for me to prove it. > if AI can reduce the time from 0 to N by 10x, the time from N to full product is also significantly reducedOnly if you assume that progress is entirely one-dimensional and there are never any trade-offs.
sentences.zh: 由家长的评论来适当反驳这一点，而不是由我来证明。 > 如果 AI 可以将从 0 到 N 的时间缩短 10 倍，那么从 N 到完整产品的时间也会显着缩短，前提是你假设进展完全是一维的，并且永远不存在任何权衡。

sentences.en: We know both those assumptions are incorrect.An extreme example: leaping out of my office window gets me down to the ground much faster than taking the stairs.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这两个假设都是不正确的。一个极端的例子：从办公室窗户跳出去比爬楼梯更快地让我落地。

sentences.en: Because of recovery time, it does not at all speed my journey home from work.
sentences.zh: 由于恢复时间的原因，它并没有加快我下班回家的速度。

sentences.en: A half-hearted and timid post.
sentences.zh: 一个半心半意和胆怯的帖子。

sentences.en: It’s very obvious it was written to avoid criticism.I think the author started writing this on a whim and couldnt bring it to a proper conclusion.
sentences.zh: 很明显，这是为了避免批评而写的。我认为作者是一时兴起才开始写这篇文章的，并没有得出一个正确的结论。

sentences.en: What i cant understand is how it managed to get such a high points on hn.
sentences.zh: 我不明白的是它是如何在 hn 上获得如此高的分数的。

sentences.en: Because the piece is completely stale—neither praise nor criticism.
sentences.zh: 因为这篇文章完全陈旧——既没有赞扬也没有批评。

sentences.en: The author’s own thoughts are so generic that we hear them every single day in our daily lives, and especially on Hacker News, in the back-and-forth between the “Coddites” and the “Vibers” crowd.My indirect take is that, since AI coding is already shrouded in uncertainty, there’s no need for it to remain in this kind of fog—this article will lose all relevance within five years and end up proving the author wrong.
sentences.zh: 作者自己的想法是如此笼统，以至于我们每天都能在日常生活中听到它们，尤其是在《黑客新闻》上，在“Coddites”和“Vibers”人群之间来来回回。我的间接看法是，由于人工智能编码已经笼罩在不确定性之中，所以没有必要让它继续处于这种迷雾中——这篇文章将在五年内失去所有相关性，最终证明作者是错的。

sentences.en: I’ll add that you still need the will and the care to drive it towards an useful product.
sentences.zh: 我要补充的是，你仍然需要意志和关怀来推动它成为一个有用的产品。

sentences.en: AI still not magically generate useful products if you don’t ask it to do it and prune the results until it approaches what you desired to create.
sentences.zh: 如果你不要求人工智能去做并修剪结果，直到它接近你想要创造的东西，人工智能仍然不会神奇地生成有用的产品。

sentences.en: I agree that the people who vibe code driven by the fear of being left behind are in a sort of self fulfilling loop.The more code is generated without understanding, the less likely it will be maintained and it will be left behind the audited code in quality and in usefulness.It's so easy to get into AI that the only thing we can be left behind is personal experience or learning.
sentences.zh: 我同意，那些因害怕落后而编写代码的人处于一种自我实现的循环中。在不理解的情况下生成的代码越多，维护它的可能性就越小，并且在质量和实用性上都会落后于经过审计的代码。进入人工智能是如此容易，我们唯一能落后的就是个人经验或学习。

sentences.en: But jumping in and spending on claude to vibe up a SaaS...pretty much anyone can do that now.
sentences.zh: 但是，投入克劳德的钱来打造 SaaS ……现在几乎任何人都可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: I am very product focused with my projects.
sentences.zh: 我的项目非常注重产品。

sentences.en: I have Claude write 100% of the code but I challenge its suggestions and make damn sure there are ways for it to verify functionality and correctness.
sentences.zh: 我让 Claude 编写了 100% 的代码，但我对它的建议提出了质疑，并确保它有办法验证功能和正确性。

sentences.en: I don't read much of the generated code but am adamant that there are tests: unit, integration and (if possible) against other implementations.
sentences.zh: 我没有阅读太多生成的代码，但坚信有测试：单元、集成和（如果可能）针对其他实现的测试。

sentences.en: And I care a LOT about performance.So far (last 6-7 months) I've built tons of stuff in my spare time: A pdf generator lib, a scheme implementation (R5RS and R7RS) with AOT compilation, a screenplay editor, a code editor, a ripgrep-like lib/engine/cli tool for fast search in a workspace, a markdown parser, a Fountain (screenplay) parser, a lib for dealing with updating apps, tooling for finding duplicate code and generating codemaps - and much more.It's been an absolute ride.
sentences.zh: 而且我非常关心性能。到目前为止（过去 6-7 个月）我在业余时间构建了大量的东西：一个 pdf 生成器库、一个带有 AOT 编译的方案实现（R5RS 和 R7RS）、一个剧本编辑器、一个代码编辑器、一个用于在工作区中快速搜索的类似 ripgrep 的 lib/engine/cli 工具、一个 markdown 解析器、一个 Fountain（剧本）解析器、一个用于处理更新应用程序的库、用于查找重复代码和生成的工具代码映射 - 以及更多。这绝对是一次旅程。

sentences.en: I build reai.no, an accounting system in Norway.
sentences.zh: 我在挪威建立了 reai.no，一个会计系统。

sentences.en: I can say with 100% certainty that if you don't know what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 我可以百分百肯定地说，如果你不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Then it will still be a mess.
sentences.zh: 那么仍然会是一团糟。

sentences.en: I throw away 90% of the code that other devs come with and also from my own prompts.I also tend to close PRs if I'm not sure it is the best solution and just ask them to start from scratch since the second time you implement something (unless you do it completely blindly) probably made you realise how you could make it simpler :)I also focus a lot on teaching devs domain knowledge.
sentences.zh: 我扔掉了其他开发人员提供的 90% 的代码以及我自己的提示。如果我不确定这是最好的解决方案，我也倾向于关闭 PR，并要求他们从头开始，因为第二次实现某些东西（除非您完全盲目地这样做）可能会让您意识到如何使其变得更简单:)我也非常注重教授开发人员领域知识。

sentences.en: Actually learning accounting so they can more independently understand how to build something "correctly".
sentences.zh: 实际上学习会计，这样他们就可以更独立地理解如何“正确”地构建一些东西。

sentences.en: I like that one “ They understand what they're asking the model to produce.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个“他们明白他们要求模型生产什么。

sentences.en: They review generated code with the same critical eye they'd apply to a junior engineer's pull request.
sentences.zh: 他们以与初级工程师拉取请求相同的挑剔眼光来审查生成的代码。

sentences.en: They bring architectural thinking to the conversation, not just feature descriptions.
sentences.zh: 他们将架构思维带入对话中，而不仅仅是功能描述。

sentences.en: They know when to push back on what the model suggests.”
sentences.zh: 他们知道何时反驳模型的建议。”

sentences.en: I use AI randomly recently and more and more see it as fantastic poc tool , also it’s really good at comparison existing tools and making some raw material for analysis Anyone who thinks this way has completely lost sight of what it means to use generative AI for software projects, namely, the concept of a tool, however sophisticated it may be, but still just a tool.
sentences.zh: 我最近随机使用人工智能，越来越多的人认为它是很棒的 poc 工具，而且它非常擅长比较现有工具并为分析提供一些原材料。任何这样认为的人都完全忽视了在软件项目中使用生成式人工智能意味着什么，即工具的概念，无论它多么复杂，但仍然只是一个工具。

sentences.en: The goal of a project can be anything from a prototype to a finished product, and using AI tools does not change what you want to achieve as the final result.
sentences.zh: 项目的目标可以是从原型到成品的任何目标，并且使用人工智能工具不会改变您想要实现的最终结果。

sentences.en: I'm tired of this "X was never the hard part" meme when in fact X (this time: prototyping) was in fact difficult.
sentences.zh: 我厌倦了这种“X 从来都不是困难的部分”的梗，而事实上 X（这次：原型设计）实际上很困难。

sentences.en: This begs the question of what the fundamentals really are.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了一个问题：基本面到底是什么？

sentences.en: There are a bajillion bootcamps and learn-x-in-a-weekend books out there, most of which seem to focus on getting you familiar with basic syntax rather than teaching the how and why.If memorising syntax and a standard library are no longer differentiators, then what exactly are you supposed to learn?
sentences.zh: 那里有无数的训练营和周末学习书籍，其中大多数似乎都专注于让你熟悉基本语法，而不是教授如何和为什么。如果记住语法和标准库不再是区别，那么你到底应该学习什么？

sentences.en: Most of this piece reads like the Claude output I have to read after every prompt, cleaned up with an /elegant-writing skill or something.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章的大部分内容读起来就像克劳德的输出，我必须在每次提示后阅读，并用/优雅的写作技巧或其他东西进行清理。

sentences.en: I'm so used to skimming text in this voice, it's hard to pay attention to this.I honestly do not understand why people do this for writing that carries their signature, essentially.
sentences.zh: 我已经习惯了用这种声音浏览文本，很难注意到这一点。老实说，我真的不明白为什么人们这样做是为了写带有他们签名的文章。

sentences.en: Do you want people to associate your name with skimmable fluff?
sentences.zh: 您想让人们将您的名字与可略读的绒毛联系起来吗？

sentences.en: We can talk to each other directly, please.
sentences.zh: 我们可以直接交谈，谢谢。

sentences.en: The machine is helpful but it doesn't have to mediate every human interaction ever.
sentences.zh: 机器很有帮助，但它不必调解每一次人类互动。

sentences.en: I’ve been a Lead Engineer in a prior life, and also led many offshore teams that executives and product managers thought were “bad”I have great results with AI assisted code bases and developmentI am the harness Can we please not share things that are 100% AI written here, at least without attribution?
